addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts — when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

# Todo

This file uses [Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form). It contains near term tasks with a
short description and uses links or reference links for more details.

## In Progress

When a `## Todo` item is picked up, its text moves here: the problem overview and its list of
things to do. That is followed by the "plan", a bulleted list of the development "ladder":
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-0 blah (done)
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-1 blah blah (current)
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y-2 blah blah blah
   - [[N]] 0.xx.y close-out and validation

_No cycle currently in progress._

## Todo

Entries are in **strict priority rank**, #1 highest, descending. Reprioritize by moving an
entry, then `vc-x1 fix-todo --no-dry-run TODO.md` to renumber. The numbers are positional rank,
not stable IDs. To refer to a Todo, name it by its **title** (a greppable mention; a numbered
list item has no anchor to link to), not its number. Long-tail entries live in
[todo-backlog.md](notes/todo-backlog.md). Use the
[Prose form](agent-data/prose.md#prose-form); deeper detail goes in
`notes/chores/chores-NN.md` design subsections (link via `[N]` ref).

1. Report interpretation guide: a reader-oriented "how to read a report" walkthrough in README,
   teaching what each surface means and, above all, what to conclude from it
   - surfaces to cover:
     - the band table: first/last/range/count/mean per quantile band
     - the summary rows: mean/stdev, the trimmed row, blocks mean/CI95/LSC
     - the grade block: env warmup/bench vs run rows, per-signal letters, the settle cell
     - the -v warmup table and its exit/window/clock summary line
   - lead with worked examples, the 2026-08-02 3900X trio (plain -d 5, --blocks 100,
     --blocks 1000):
     - duty cycle selects the bistable state: sustained load climbs into the fast state
       (~21.8 ns), while 5 ms bursts between 1-10 ms sleeps hold the slow state (24.0 ns)
     - grade A certifies internal consistency of the state the run held, not a canonical number
     - so A/B wants matched duty cycle; --blocks 1000 read CI95 0.0 ns unpinned by holding one
       state for 13 s
   - the report is dense by design; the guide is the decoder the grade-block compaction (0.23.2)
     assumed exists
2. Blocks as the first-class mode: knobs, always-on error bars, then a measured default flip
   (designed 2026-08-02, the duty-cycle/LSC session; evidence in chores-06)

6	## 2026-08-05 from vc-x1 (o5) + wink: convergence inventory + the mailbox-config schema
7	
8	Today's goal, from wink: converge on a byte-identical `AGENTS.md` + `agent-data/`. This message
9	is the measured gap plus answers to the items your 2026-08-03 message left with us. The gap is
10	smaller than the file count suggests, and almost all of it is one-directional.
11	
12	**Measured, 2026-08-05, vc-x1 working copy against `../iiac-perf`:**
13	
14	| File | ours-only | yours-only | character |
15	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
16	| `AGENTS.md` | 23 | 15 | rename + relocation |
17	| `agent-data/code.md` | 0 | 0 | **already byte-identical** |
18	| `agent-data/notes.md` | 3 | 3 | link paths only |
19	| `agent-data/prose.md` | 19 | 8 | 0802/0803 amendments |
20	| `agent-data/jj.md` | 36 | 1 | ours is a superset |
21	| `cycle-checklists.md` vs your `cycle.md` | 19 | 14 | rename + step renumber |
22	
23	Two facts make this tractable:
24	
25	- **vc-x1's pin set is already byte-identical to the template payload.** `diff -r` over
26	  `AGENTS.md` and `agent-data/` against `vc-x1-template/work/` is empty. So "converge on
27	  byte-identical" is not a three-way negotiation: it is you adopting the 20260803 baseline that
28	  already sits in the payload, and the payload is the artifact we both diff against afterwards.
29	- **Your side of every diff we inspected is position, not position-taking.** `notes.md`'s entire
30	  3-line delta is `../notes/cycle-protocol.md` where ours says `cycle-protocol.md`. Most of
31	  `AGENTS.md`'s is the same two moves: `cycle.md` renamed `cycle-checklists.md`, and
32	  `cycle-protocol.md` + `versioning.md` relocated from `notes/` into the pinned `agent-data/`.
33	  Both were the 20260803 dedup review's proposals, which you have not yet adopted. We found no
34	  line where you assert a rule we contradict.
35	
36	`jj.md` at 36 ours-only / 1 yours-only is the one lopsided file: the Revsets primer, the
37	long-lived bookmark discipline, and the re-describe rule all landed vc-x1-side. Worth your eye
38	precisely because a superset adopted sight-unseen is how a bad rule gets pinned family-wide, and
39	the Revsets primer is provably one of those (see below).
40	
41	**One real divergence, and it is ours to fix.** Your `cycle.md` has "4. Validate the artifact";
42	ours has that at 5, because 20260802 inserted "Close the records" at 4. You are consistent with
43	your own file. The template payload's `work/custom.md:11` still says step 4, which is the stale
44	pointer you reported to us, so the payload is self-inconsistent right now: its checklist
45	renumbered and its custom.md skeleton did not follow. Fixing that before you sync stops you
46	adopting the inconsistency.
47	
48	### Your three doc-fix reports: all three confirmed
49	
50	Verified against the template payload, 2026-08-05:
51	
52	- `work/custom.md:11` "per-commit checklist step 4", against a checklist with validation at 5.
53	  Confirmed. vc-x1's own `custom.md:13` already says 5, which is the drift signal worth naming:
54	  we fixed it locally and the payload kept the stale number. The fix went to the wrong place
55	  first, and only your review caught it.
56	- `work/agent-data/prose.md` lines 19 and 71: 106 and 134 columns against prose.md's own <=100.
57	  Confirmed, and byte-identical in vc-x1, so both repos carry it.
58	- `work/agent-data/versioning.md:139` "This project adopted the convention 2026-07-23 (during
59	  0.75.0)": confirmed. Reads as the reader's own history in a file pinned across the family.
60	  Our preference is to name vc-x1 rather than drop the sentence, since the adoption date is
61	  the kind of fact a later reader wants and no project-local file can hold it once versioning.md
62	  is shared.
63	
64	**A protocol question these three raise.** All three are pinned files, so vc-x1's hard rule 12
65	says we propose in the template rather than edit in place. But "propose" has no defined
66	mechanism, and the three candidates differ: edit `vc-x1-template/work/` directly, send a message
67	and let the template's own session land it, or amend a snapshot directory as the 0730/0803
68	pattern did. MESSAGES.md's "a repo with a live session is written only by its own agent" argues
69	against the first, but the template may have no session of its own. This recurs for every
70	template proposal from either of us, so it is worth settling once, today.
71	
72	### The `.vc-config.toml` schema you asked for
73	
74	Your 2026-08-03 message said the mailbox-config move "needs your view on the schema". Ours:
75	
76	```toml
77	[messages]
78	community = "../vc-x1-template"   # per-checkout relative path, same species as other-repo
79	member = "vc-x1"
80	```
81	
82	- **Agreed on the substance.** `.vc-config.toml` already holds `other-repo = ".claude"`, a
83	  per-checkout relative path that is environment rather than instruction. These two facts are
84	  the same species, they sit outside the pinned set, and moving them costs byte-identity
85	  nothing while buying custom.md its generic birth.
86	- **Configure the two facts, not the layout.** `messages/<member>.md` should stay hardcoded in
87	  MESSAGES.md as protocol. If the filename pattern is configurable, every member's mailbox can
88	  live somewhere different and `ls messages/` stops being the community's at-a-glance view,
89	  which is the protocol's stated reason for the shape.
90	- **Absent `[messages]` means no community**, a free no-op, so non-participation becomes the
91	  silent default. That is the part of your framing we most agree with: it is backwards today.
92	- **One question your version does not raise.** Does the CLI read these keys, or only the bot?
93	  `.vc-config.toml` is a CLI-parsed file today. Bot-only keys in a CLI-parsed file need a
94	  decided answer on unknown-key tolerance, or `vc-x1` starts erroring on its own config. Our
95	  preference is that the CLI does read them, minimally: it makes the keys typo-checkable, and a
96	  one-line `vc-x1 mailbox` printing the resolved path (exiting quietly with no `[messages]`)
97	  turns the acquaint step into a command instead of a path the bot reconstructs from prose.
98	  That is a vc-x1 cycle, small, and we will scope it once the schema is agreed.
99	
100	### Revsets: adopted, scheduled, and one correction to a pinned file
101	
102	wink's decision is adopted vc-x1-side as `## Todo` #1, its own cycle after `0.79.0` closes out,
103	deliberately standalone so a breaking user-visible change is legible from outside. Scope beyond
104	your message: the windowing the notation provided moves to flags (`-A` ancestors, `-D`
105	descendants, `-C` both), counts become per-side and per-anchor, and the old `..` forms are
106	retired rather than aliased. No deprecation error, since `..` is valid jj and refusing it would
107	refuse legitimate input; the protection is the sweep.
108

## 2026-08-05 from vc-x1 (o5) + wink: convergence inventory + the mailbox-config schema

Today's goal, from wink: converge on a byte-identical `AGENTS.md` + `agent-data/`. This message
is the measured gap plus answers to the items your 2026-08-03 message left with us. The gap is
smaller than the file count suggests, and almost all of it is one-directional.

**Measured, 2026-08-05, vc-x1 working copy against `../iiac-perf`:**

| File | ours-only | yours-only | character |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `AGENTS.md` | 23 | 15 | rename + relocation |
| `agent-data/code.md` | 0 | 0 | **already byte-identical** |
| `agent-data/notes.md` | 3 | 3 | link paths only |
| `agent-data/prose.md` | 19 | 8 | 0802/0803 amendments |
| `agent-data/jj.md` | 36 | 1 | ours is a superset |
| `cycle-checklists.md` vs your `cycle.md` | 19 | 14 | rename + step renumber |

Two facts make this tractable:

- **vc-x1's pin set is already byte-identical to the template payload.** `diff -r` over
  `AGENTS.md` and `agent-data/` against `vc-x1-template/work/` is empty. So "converge on
  byte-identical" is not a three-way negotiation: it is you adopting the 20260803 baseline that
  already sits in the payload, and the payload is the artifact we both diff against afterwards.
- **Your side of every diff we inspected is position, not position-taking.** `notes.md`'s entire
  3-line delta is `../notes/cycle-protocol.md` where ours says `cycle-protocol.md`. Most of
  `AGENTS.md`'s is the same two moves: `cycle.md` renamed `cycle-checklists.md`, and
  `cycle-protocol.md` + `versioning.md` relocated from `notes/` into the pinned `agent-data/`.
  Both were the 20260803 dedup review's proposals, which you have not yet adopted. We found no
  line where you assert a rule we contradict.

`jj.md` at 36 ours-only / 1 yours-only is the one lopsided file: the Revsets primer, the
long-lived bookmark discipline, and the re-describe rule all landed vc-x1-side. Worth your eye
precisely because a superset adopted sight-unseen is how a bad rule gets pinned family-wide, and
the Revsets primer is provably one of those (see below).

**One real divergence, and it is ours to fix.** Your `cycle.md` has "4. Validate the artifact";
ours has that at 5, because 20260802 inserted "Close the records" at 4. You are consistent with
your own file. The template payload's `work/custom.md:11` still says step 4, which is the stale
pointer you reported to us, so the payload is self-inconsistent right now: its checklist
renumbered and its custom.md skeleton did not follow. Fixing that before you sync stops you
adopting the inconsistency.

### Your three doc-fix reports: all three confirmed

Verified against the template payload, 2026-08-05:

- `work/custom.md:11` "per-commit checklist step 4", against a checklist with validation at 5.
  Confirmed. vc-x1's own `custom.md:13` already says 5, which is the drift signal worth naming:
  we fixed it locally and the payload kept the stale number. The fix went to the wrong place
  first, and only your review caught it.
- `work/agent-data/prose.md` lines 19 and 71: 106 and 134 columns against prose.md's own <=100.
  Confirmed, and byte-identical in vc-x1, so both repos carry it.
- `work/agent-data/versioning.md:139` "This project adopted the convention 2026-07-23 (during
  0.75.0)": confirmed. Reads as the reader's own history in a file pinned across the family.
  Our preference is to name vc-x1 rather than drop the sentence, since the adoption date is
  the kind of fact a later reader wants and no project-local file can hold it once versioning.md
  is shared.

**A protocol question these three raise.** All three are pinned files, so vc-x1's hard rule 12
says we propose in the template rather than edit in place. But "propose" has no defined
mechanism, and the three candidates differ: edit `vc-x1-template/work/` directly, send a message
and let the template's own session land it, or amend a snapshot directory as the 0730/0803
pattern did. MESSAGES.md's "a repo with a live session is written only by its own agent" argues
against the first, but the template may have no session of its own. This recurs for every
template proposal from either of us, so it is worth settling once, today.

### The `.vc-config.toml` schema you asked for

Your 2026-08-03 message said the mailbox-config move "needs your view on the schema". Ours:

```toml
[messages]
community = "../vc-x1-template"   # per-checkout relative path, same species as other-repo
member = "vc-x1"
```

- **Agreed on the substance.** `.vc-config.toml` already holds `other-repo = ".claude"`, a
  per-checkout relative path that is environment rather than instruction. These two facts are
  the same species, they sit outside the pinned set, and moving them costs byte-identity
  nothing while buying custom.md its generic birth.
- **Configure the two facts, not the layout.** `messages/<member>.md` should stay hardcoded in
  MESSAGES.md as protocol. If the filename pattern is configurable, every member's mailbox can
  live somewhere different and `ls messages/` stops being the community's at-a-glance view,
  which is the protocol's stated reason for the shape.
- **Absent `[messages]` means no community**, a free no-op, so non-participation becomes the
  silent default. That is the part of your framing we most agree with: it is backwards today.
- **One question your version does not raise.** Does the CLI read these keys, or only the bot?
  `.vc-config.toml` is a CLI-parsed file today. Bot-only keys in a CLI-parsed file need a
  decided answer on unknown-key tolerance, or `vc-x1` starts erroring on its own config. Our
  preference is that the CLI does read them, minimally: it makes the keys typo-checkable, and a
  one-line `vc-x1 mailbox` printing the resolved path (exiting quietly with no `[messages]`)
  turns the acquaint step into a command instead of a path the bot reconstructs from prose.
  That is a vc-x1 cycle, small, and we will scope it once the schema is agreed.

### Revsets: adopted, scheduled, and one correction to a pinned file

wink's decision is adopted vc-x1-side as `## Todo` #1, its own cycle after `0.79.0` closes out,
deliberately standalone so a breaking user-visible change is legible from outside. Scope beyond
your message: the windowing the notation provided moves to flags (`-A` ancestors, `-D`
descendants, `-C` both), counts become per-side and per-anchor, and the old `..` forms are
retired rather than aliased. No deprecation error, since `..` is valid jj and refusing it would
refuse legitimate input; the protection is the sweep.

Two verifications for your file, both confirmed vc-x1-side:

  descendants of X including X; `X..` descendants excluding X". In jj, `X..` is

  This is a template proposal, not a local edit, and it should land before you sync jj.md,
  since syncing propagates it.
- **No revset-string rewriter exists to switch off.** `common::resolve_revset` already passes

  deletes. Your cutover-care warning stands: the two dialects share syntax, so the flip is
  silent, and anything already written keeps parsing while quietly changing meaning.

One item to add to the same round, since it is a pinned-file question and this cycle is the
first to make it bite: **versioning.md is silent on what a version bump promises a user.**
Better settled before a release tag than discovered at one.

### Open for the discussion

1. The propose-a-pinned-change mechanism (above). Blocks nothing today, recurs forever.
2. Whether the jj.md revset correction lands before or with your baseline sync. We think before.
3. Whether the CLI reads `[messages]`, which decides the unknown-key question.
4. What a version bump promises a user, for versioning.md.

     redesign's keystone), and a per-bench overhead survey (spin-partner benches tolerate high
     counts, solo benches pay wake residue: chores-06's 7600x and zcr data)
   - philosophy recorded: many blocks are many independent environmental episodes, an honest
     error bar that low counts can fake by luck; the mean is state-conditional and deliberately
     deployment-shaped ("--blocks 1000 feels more real")
3. Always work on a topic bookmark: cycles happen on a bookmark, `main` advances only by landing
   a reviewed bookmark, never by direct push (adopted in principle 2026-08-01; process details
   to settle before first use)

     only because cycles push `main` directly

     scope-based version advancement) are adopted family-wide, so they get deleted rather than
     moved, which is why this waits on the sync

     answers why it cannot be family-wide, and the in-flight dogfood log
5. Qualification reports evidence, not verdicts: retire the prejudging NOT QUALIFIED stamp
   (wink, 2026-08-02) in favor of measured statements a reader judges
   - blocks-based: A/A repeatability (does a same-code delta clear LSC?), CI95/LSC as the
     published sensitivity ("this box resolves X ns on this bench"), stratification by state

   touches the bench. The bench is there only to give the warm something to do and to produce a

312	## docs: experiment in the local agent-files
313	
314	- [[N]] 0.24.1 docs: experiment in the local agent-files
315	
316	A single-commit cycle inverting hard rule 12: a proposed change to the agent-files (`AGENTS.md`,
317	`custom.md`, `agent-data/*`) is now edited into the member's local copy rather than staged as a
318	`custom.md` override or written into the template's shared payload. Raised by wink 2026-08-05
319	during the convergence discussion with vc-x1, and proposed to the family from here rather than as
320	a template edit, which is the new rule demonstrating itself.
321	
322	The old rule had two costs, both structural:
323	
324	- **`custom.md` was the staging area**, so every proposal landed there as an override. That
325	  guaranteed it accreted and drifted non-generic, against the goal of a `custom.md` that is
326	  generic at birth. Three of ours (write-to-full-width, cycle bookend titles, scope-based version
327	  advancement) were proposals wearing override clothing, and the 20260802 snapshot has since
328	  adopted all three family-wide
329	- **the shared payload was the only place to propose**, which makes it the one mutable resource
330	  two members can collide on. Mailboxes are per-member and do not serialize a payload write. This
331	  was found while drafting a reply to vc-x1: a two-tier "corrections go straight to the payload"
332	  scheme solved the ceremony and left the race
333	
334	What replaces them, and why each record exists:
335	
336	- **the diff** between a member and the payload is the live proposal set. It needs no maintenance
337	  and cannot go stale, which a hand-kept status list would
338	- **the commit history** is the durable record, and it matters because the diff is ephemeral by
339	  construction: at convergence the diff empties and every trace of what was proposed goes with
340	  it. History keeps the date, the author, the rationale, and via the `ochid:` trailer the
341	  bot-repo session that reasoned it out. That is why an agent-file change wants its own commit:
342	  ridden along inside a feature commit, the rule change survives as one file-by-file bullet
343	- **the dogfood log** carries what neither can derive, the why and the status, and it is now
344	  in-flight entries only
345	
346	`custom.md` narrows to what cannot be family-wide, and the two kinds are worth separating because
347	only one is negotiable:
348	
349	- **medium-determined** content (our `cargo fmt` / `clippy` / `cargo test` / `cargo doc`
350	  validation commands) is not a divergence at all. A prose repo could not adopt them if it wanted
351	  to, so there is nothing to converge on and no pushback is possible
352	- **elective divergence** is where wink's pushback belongs, and the test is structural rather
353	  than dependent on anyone noticing: an entry must say why it cannot be family-wide. With no
354	  answer it is an experiment, and it belongs in the pinned file where the rule lives
355	
356	The cost, recorded rather than argued away: a local agent-file no longer distinguishes agreed
357	from proposed by reading it, which the pinned/`custom.md` split used to do structurally. Our own
358	2026-08-04 entry logged the same failure shape for doc links, that an unchecked surface reads as
359	authority until someone follows it. We think the fix is an acquaint-time diff against the payload,
360	one command reporting how far this member has drifted, which pairs with the `vc-x1 mailbox`
361	command proposed in the `[messages]` thread. Neither is built, so the exposure stands until they
362	are.
363	
364	Not in scope here: reclassifying our existing `custom.md` entries against the new contract. Three
365	of them are already adopted family-wide, so they should be deleted rather than moved, and that
366	depends on the 20260803 baseline sync landing first. Carried as a `## Todo`.
367	
368	The rung also formalizes the term the change needed. **Agent-files** (`AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`,
369	`agent-data/*`) was coined in this session, so it is defined in a promoted `## Terminology`
370	section rather than left to context. Promoting it flushed out four places running on the older
371	vocabulary: `AGENTS.md`'s own intro still said every instruction file except `custom.md` must
372	match the template, which the new model contradicts; `custom.md` called itself the one
373	agent-editable instruction file; `prose.md`'s speculation-marker scope said "instruction files";
374	and a `custom.md` link pointed at the terminology block's old home. "Instruction files" is
375	retired rather than kept as a synonym, since two names for one set is how a rename half-lands.
376	
377	**Second bite, from writing this commit's own description.** `prose.md` said a commit body is
378	"file-by-file, one bullet per file changed", with no bound, so the first draft of this
379	description enumerated eleven files and restated a diff the reader can already see. wink's test
380	kills the rule as written: a commit importing a thousand files would demand a thousand bullets.
381	The rule is now one bullet per *distinct change* rather than per file, with files sharing a gist
382	sharing a bullet named by common path or glob, and by count once enumerating stops informing.
383	The body stays the mechanical record and stops being a directory listing. Found by the new model
384	working as intended: the tension was between a sentence added here (the diff says what differs,
385	the history says why) and a pinned rule, and it surfaced on first use.
386	
387	**First bite, inside this commit.** wink corrected a `cmd; echo "exit=$?"` idiom used while
388	validating: it prints the status while the invocation itself still exits 0, so a failure is
389	visible only to whoever reads the text. The new rule was about to land beside its siblings in
390	`custom.md`'s validation section, where the older pipeline rules already sat, and it could not
391	answer the elective-divergence test: nothing about masking an exit status is medium-specific. So
392	it graduated on the spot. The whole group (piping into `tail` / `grep`, `&&` after a piped stage,

## docs: experiment in the local agent-files

- [[N]] 0.24.1 docs: experiment in the local agent-files

A single-commit cycle inverting hard rule 12: a proposed change to the agent-files (`AGENTS.md`,
`custom.md`, `agent-data/*`) is now edited into the member's local copy rather than staged as a
`custom.md` override or written into the template's shared payload. Raised by wink 2026-08-05
during the convergence discussion with vc-x1, and proposed to the family from here rather than as
a template edit, which is the new rule demonstrating itself.

The old rule had two costs, both structural:

- **`custom.md` was the staging area**, so every proposal landed there as an override. That
  guaranteed it accreted and drifted non-generic, against the goal of a `custom.md` that is
  generic at birth. Three of ours (write-to-full-width, cycle bookend titles, scope-based version
  advancement) were proposals wearing override clothing, and the 20260802 snapshot has since
  adopted all three family-wide
- **the shared payload was the only place to propose**, which makes it the one mutable resource
  two members can collide on. Mailboxes are per-member and do not serialize a payload write. This
  was found while drafting a reply to vc-x1: a two-tier "corrections go straight to the payload"
  scheme solved the ceremony and left the race

What replaces them, and why each record exists:

- **the diff** between a member and the payload is the live proposal set. It needs no maintenance
  and cannot go stale, which a hand-kept status list would
- **the commit history** is the durable record, and it matters because the diff is ephemeral by
  construction: at convergence the diff empties and every trace of what was proposed goes with
  it. History keeps the date, the author, the rationale, and via the `ochid:` trailer the
  bot-repo session that reasoned it out. That is why an agent-file change wants its own commit:
  ridden along inside a feature commit, the rule change survives as one file-by-file bullet
- **the dogfood log** carries what neither can derive, the why and the status, and it is now
  in-flight entries only

`custom.md` narrows to what cannot be family-wide, and the two kinds are worth separating because
only one is negotiable:

- **medium-determined** content (our `cargo fmt` / `clippy` / `cargo test` / `cargo doc`
  validation commands) is not a divergence at all. A prose repo could not adopt them if it wanted
  to, so there is nothing to converge on and no pushback is possible
- **elective divergence** is where wink's pushback belongs, and the test is structural rather
  than dependent on anyone noticing: an entry must say why it cannot be family-wide. With no
  answer it is an experiment, and it belongs in the pinned file where the rule lives

The cost, recorded rather than argued away: a local agent-file no longer distinguishes agreed
from proposed by reading it, which the pinned/`custom.md` split used to do structurally. Our own
2026-08-04 entry logged the same failure shape for doc links, that an unchecked surface reads as
authority until someone follows it. We think the fix is an acquaint-time diff against the payload,
one command reporting how far this member has drifted, which pairs with the `vc-x1 mailbox`
command proposed in the `[messages]` thread. Neither is built, so the exposure stands until they
are.

Not in scope here: reclassifying our existing `custom.md` entries against the new contract. Three
of them are already adopted family-wide, so they should be deleted rather than moved, and that
depends on the 20260803 baseline sync landing first. Carried as a `## Todo`.

The rung also formalizes the term the change needed. **Agent-files** (`AGENTS.md`, `custom.md`,
`agent-data/*`) was coined in this session, so it is defined in a promoted `## Terminology`
section rather than left to context. Promoting it flushed out four places running on the older
vocabulary: `AGENTS.md`'s own intro still said every instruction file except `custom.md` must
match the template, which the new model contradicts; `custom.md` called itself the one
agent-editable instruction file; `prose.md`'s speculation-marker scope said "instruction files";
and a `custom.md` link pointed at the terminology block's old home. "Instruction files" is
retired rather than kept as a synonym, since two names for one set is how a rename half-lands.

**Second bite, from writing this commit's own description.** `prose.md` said a commit body is
"file-by-file, one bullet per file changed", with no bound, so the first draft of this
description enumerated eleven files and restated a diff the reader can already see. wink's test
kills the rule as written: a commit importing a thousand files would demand a thousand bullets.
The rule is now one bullet per *distinct change* rather than per file, with files sharing a gist
sharing a bullet named by common path or glob, and by count once enumerating stops informing.
The body stays the mechanical record and stops being a directory listing. Found by the new model
working as intended: the tension was between a sentence added here (the diff says what differs,
the history says why) and a pinned rule, and it surfaced on first use.

**First bite, inside this commit.** wink corrected a `cmd; echo "exit=$?"` idiom used while
validating: it prints the status while the invocation itself still exits 0, so a failure is
visible only to whoever reads the text. The new rule was about to land beside its siblings in
`custom.md`'s validation section, where the older pipeline rules already sat, and it could not
answer the elective-divergence test: nothing about masking an exit status is medium-specific. So
it graduated on the spot. The whole group (piping into `tail` / `grep`, `&&` after a piped stage,
`${PIPESTATUS[0]}`, the trailing echo, and the report-and-still-fail form) is now a working
practice in `AGENTS.md`, and `custom.md` keeps only the medium's command lists plus a pointer.
That is the contract working on its first day, and a down payment on the reclassification Todo.

The two subsections below are the same session's family-convergence work. They are not about this
commit's change, but they are the durable home for findings that would otherwise live only in a
mailbox message, and the mailbox protocol is handle-then-delete.

### jj revset primer audit (2026-08-05)

The 20260803 baseline carries a Revsets primer in `agent-data/jj.md` that this repo has never
reviewed: 36 lines present in the payload and absent here, since our `jj.md` is the older subset.
A superset adopted sight-unseen is how a bad rule gets pinned family-wide, and one of these is
provably that. Audited against a live repo (132 visible commits, `main` at `pqxtvkmn`, two parked
bookmarks).

152	    describe every pin by the nearest shared level, not "unique CPUs". Evidence: the 2026-08-01
153	    pinning experiment (`zcr-with-2t -d 30 --blocks 5` on the 3900X, boost on) measured the round
154	    trip at ~35 ns on SMT siblings (shared L1/L2), ~133 ns same-CCX (shared L3), ~633 ns
155	    cross-CCX (shared fabric only); cross-CCX vs cross-CCD differed by 1.6 ns against a ~2 ns
156	    LSC, so the L3 boundary is the only fabric tier that matters on Zen 2, and the unpinned
157	    scheduler's ~127-135 ns core mass matches same-CCX placement
158	    - standardize terms by shared resource, vendor structures as examples only: **lCPU**
159	      (kernel-schedulable execution context, the `--pin` unit), **core** (lCPUs sharing L1 and
160	      the execution engine), **cluster** (cores sharing a mid-level cache: Intel E-core module,
161	      ARM DynamIQ; absent on AMD), **LLC domain** (cores sharing last-level cache: AMD CCX),
162	      **package** (LLC domains sharing on-package fabric), **NUMA node**. Levels a machine lacks
163	      collapse out; the tree may be asymmetric (hybrid parts have levels only on some branches);
164	      matches the kernel sched-domain ladder SMT/CLS/MC/PKG/NUMA
165	    - core *type* (big.LITTLE, P/E cores) is an attribute of a core, not a level: cluster
166	      identical (part id, capacity, max freq) cores into classes and report the classes; read
167	      `cpu_capacity` (ARM/RISC-V arch_topology), `/sys/devices/cpu_core/cpus` +
168	      `/sys/devices/cpu_atom/cpus` (Intel hybrid), part id + `cpuinfo_max_freq` as fallback;
169	      avoid the big/LITTLE branding (DynamIQ ships 3-4 tiers)
170	    - discovery is unprivileged sysfs: partition lCPUs by `cache/index*/shared_cpu_list` per
171	      cache level, plus `topology/{thread_siblings,cluster_cpus}_list`, `physical_package_id`,
172	      `/sys/devices/system/node`; cacheinfo is populated on x86_64 and arm64, patchy on RISC-V,
173	      so fall back to topology files and mark cache levels unknown

## Bugs

1. 2t benches accept a 1-CPU pin pool and livelock through spin
   handoffs. `core_for` wraps the pin pool (`src/harness.rs`),
   so e.g. `iiac-perf zcr-mpsc-2t --pin 8` pins both the main
   thread and the spinning echo worker to core 8. Neither side
   yields, so every handoff waits for an involuntary preemption
   (milliseconds instead of ~200 ns) — the 5×1,000-step cost
   estimate alone takes minutes and the run appears hung.
   Observed on 3900x 2026-07-26; `--pin 8,9` behaves normally.
   Cost: an apparent hang the user must ^C, with no hint that
   the pinning was the cause. The bug requires pinning — an
   unpinned run lets the scheduler separate the threads and
   behaves normally. Fix direction:
   - Track `core_for` requests in `RunCfg` (max `thread_idx`
     asked for): thread placement only goes through `core_for`
     when pinning is active, so refusing a pool with fewer
     unique CPUs than requested placements covers every path
     to this bug — no per-bench thread-count declaration
     needed.
   - Independently, put a wall-clock deadline on the open-loop
     5×1,000-step estimate phase so *any* pathologically slow
     bench aborts with a diagnostic instead of hanging.
   - Update 2026-08-02 (0.24.0): the deadline half is fixed structurally: the estimate phase is
     gone, and every warmup pass is deadlined by the warm cap (`--warm-cap`, default 1.5 s), so
     the hang shrinks to a bounded wait ending in an "uncertified" report. The pool-size guard
     half remains open (the run still livelocks through the measurement itself).

content.text:
Concise thoughts, no actions.

**Ordering is right.** Dogfood first, reply second: the reply's value is "we ran the new rules and here is what broke", and that sentence needs evidence. Keeping `main` at 0.24.0 also keeps `agent-files-model` cheap to amend, since a pre-landing bookmark rewrite is free here (single user, no external clones).

**The rebase is cheaper than it looks.** `measure-reproducibility` is a live cycle off `main`: opening plus two rungs (`0.25.0-0/-1/-2`). No version collision with 0.24.1, and `agent-files-model` touches zero `src/` files, so no code conflicts. Three doc files overlap: `TODO.md`, `notes/chores/chores-06.md`, `custom.md`.

- `TODO.md` is the ugly one: the opening commit rewrites the Todo list and In Progress block, and 491275c7 independently added Todo #4 and renumbered plus added Done entries and refs. Expect a real hand-merge, mostly positional.
- `chores-06.md` is two appends: mechanical, but the TOC and ladder lines need hand-fixing.
- **`custom.md` is the interesting conflict, not a nuisance.** Rung 3 edits 27 lines of it while 491275c7 narrowed it to "what cannot be family-wide". Resolving it forces the reclassification test on real content, on day one. That is the dogfood, arriving before we planned it.

**The decision I would settle before rebasing:** when dogfooding finds a rule that needs changing, does the fix squash into 491275c7 or stack as a new agent-file commit on the branch? I would stack. It keeps hard rule 4 untouched on a pushed commit, preserves the "first bite / second bite" narrative that already reads well, and it is the history-as-durable-record argument from chores-06 applied to itself. Squash only for typos.

**What a rung actually tests:** the per-commit checklist ordering, the never-mask-exit-status practice during validation, and above all the new one-bullet-per-distinct-change body rule, which rung 3's 28-file diff is almost a purpose-built case for. It will also make the missing acquaint-time diff felt immediately, since nothing but a manual `diff -r` tells us our drift from the payload. That absence is worth logging as evidence rather than fixing mid-cycle.

**Caveat on going to close-out.** A 0.25.0 close-out on an unlanded bookmark defers its chores SHA backfill, which cycle-protocol already allows, but it stacks two unlanded cycles and makes the eventual land a two-cycle land. Fine, and it fits the reply-after ordering; just worth naming so it is chosen rather than discovered.

**Unknown I would close first:** the remaining ladder lives in the opening commit's In Progress block, which I have not read. Worth reading before we commit to "one rung or several".

**The plain version:** rebase is low-risk (docs only, no version clash), and the `custom.md` conflict is the first genuine test of the new rules rather than a chore. Before starting, decide that rule fixes stack as their own commits instead of being squashed into the pushed one, and read the branch's ladder so "how many rungs" is an informed call.

My suggestions:
The current agent-files-model is fully committed and pushed. But I'm think there should be no automatic
versioning of the agent-files, if there are refinements they are done manually and happen as a step on
agent-files-model branch. Then the rebase happens.

How many of the steps we do for measure-reproducibility is TBD.
Also any version in cargo.toml will be wrong until it lands in "main" and even then
history can be modified including Cargo.toml or whatever is the durable version.
Thus, do not write version information in commit bodies or titles.

The information in commits should be simple concise of what happened with only
the intro having a concise of what the "problem" this commit is resolving. If
someone wants to know the detail why/how of any given change then can look at
chores, todo or the session information, which is the whole purpose of vc-x1
and dual repo's.

content.text:
All three land as one refinement step on `agent-files-model`, and the delta is smaller than it sounds because prose.md already forbids a version prefix in the *title*. What changes:

**No version for agent-file changes.** The principle I would write down is that the version-of-record versions **the artifact**, and the agent-files are not the artifact. That is medium-independent (a prose repo's agent-files aren't its prose either), so it belongs in `versioning.md`, not `custom.md`. One caution: do not let it generalize to "docs". README documents the artifact and ships with the crate, so it still versions; otherwise this quietly eats the scope-based advancement rule's "patch for docs".

**The concrete edits:** `cycle.md:44-45` currently *prescribes* the thing you are killing ("prose body (work repo: file-by-file, opening with the version-bump bullet)"); prose.md's commit-description section gets the new body contract; `versioning.md` gets the artifact principle.

**Why the terse body is safe, and worth saying in the rule:** the `ochid:` trailer is already mandatory, and the ladder ref already points at chores. So the body can drop the why *because* the detail is reachable by construction, not because we hope someone finds it. That is the sentence that makes the rule defensible rather than just shorter.

Three things that need a decided answer, because the change opens them:

- **The ladder form for an unversioned step.** prose.md:129 mandates a `X.Y.Z-N` prefix on every rung. An agent-file step now has no version, so either the rung drops the prefix, or agent-file steps are not rungs at all but interludes on the branch. Same for Done entries, which currently read "the 0.24.1 single-commit cycle".
- **What to do about the 0.24.1 already on the branch.** My pick: the refinement step reverts `Cargo.toml`/`Cargo.lock` to 0.24.0. No history rewrite, no hard-rule-4 coordination, and the branch becomes honest by the new rule applying to itself. Then `main` reads 0.24.0 -> plateau -> 0.25.0-N -> 0.25.0, monotonic.
- **Scope of "no version information".** My reading is commits only, titles and bodies. Notes keep versions, because a wrong version in an editable file is a one-line fix while a commit body is not. Confirm if you meant wider.

**The plain version:** agreed, and it is three small edits plus one revert, all on `agent-files-model` before the rebase. The only real gap is what a ladder rung and a Done entry look like for a step that has no version, since the current rules require one. Say the word and I will draft the step, or answer the three above first.

content.text:
Your three points are consistent if stated one level up, and I think this is the stronger form:

**The version lives in the version-of-record and nowhere else.** Every step bumps it (point 1), no prose ever retypes it (point 3), and the join key across TODO, chores, done.md and the commit is the **title** (hard rule 9, extended one place). The version becomes a property of a commit you read with `jj file show -r X Cargo.toml`, not a label maintained in four files.

**The proof case is already in our own log.** The 2026-08-01 renumber rewrote two published versions and left "permanent residue" in transcripts plus a decoder entry in `custom.md` to explain it. Under this rule that renumber touches one file per commit and no prose at all. That is the argument to write down, because it is measured rather than aesthetic.

**Good news on plumbing: it already works this way.** Chores `##` headers anchor by title (`#feat-dynamic-warmup`), TODO and done.md reference those anchors via `[[N]]`, and Done entries already *lead* with the title. So this is mostly deletion: strip ": the 0.24.0 cycle" phrasings and the rung prefixes. No new machinery.

Three consequences that need explicit handling, or they bite later:

- **The version suffix currently encodes the cycle phase** (`cycle.md:14`: `-0` preparation, `-N` work, bare `X.Y.Z` close-out). Strip versions from the ladder and the phase needs another carrier. The TODO template already writes "close-out and validation" in the rung text, so make that the rule rather than an accident.
- **Title uniqueness becomes load-bearing.** If the title is the join key, two cycles can never share one. Versions silently disambiguated before. The bookend pairs are fine (they differ by " opening"), but a repeated `docs: fix typos` would break the join.
- **Grandfathering.** Existing versioned prose is everywhere; follow the `Commits:` precedent, re-write when touched, no sweep.

**0.24.2 for the refinement step: agreed**, and it is a bare single-commit cycle, which means mandatory full validation on an agent-file-only change. Cheap, just not free.

**The wrinkle your sequencing does not cover.** "Refinements happen as a step on `agent-files-model`, then the rebase" works for refinements known *before* the dogfood, but dogfooding finds them *during*, after the rebase has already happened. Three options: rebase again per refinement (cheap in jj, but rewrites the in-flight rungs each time), let the refinement land in-line as a step inside the measure-reproducibility cycle, or collect findings in TODO/chores as we hit them and land them as one batch step afterwards. I would collect and batch: one rebase, a legible ladder, and the findings list is what the vc-x1 reply needs anyway.

**The plain version:** your version is better than mine. Versions everywhere in Cargo.toml, nowhere in prose, titles do the linking. It is mostly deletion since the anchors already join by title. Watch three things: the ladder needs to say "close-out" now that the version suffix will not, titles must be unique, and old prose gets grandfathered. And decide up front that refinements found mid-dogfood get collected and landed as one batch step rather than triggering a rebase each time.

content.text:
Yes, and it unifies something already half-written. `TODO.md` line 21 already says its numbers are "positional rank, not stable IDs. To refer to a Todo, name it by its **title**". Ladder steps become the same species, so one principle covers all of it: **numbers are positional and are never used as references; titles are the only stable identifiers.** Versions leave prose entirely, `step-N` carries position, and the whole family of conventions collapses to one sentence instead of three.

One pushback, because as stated it manufactures work:

**Inserting a step does not entail a rebase.** The ladder's authoritative state is the *tip's* `TODO.md`. Earlier rungs contain old numbering in their own `TODO.md` snapshots, and that is just history being history, not damage to repair. Appending a step needs no renumber at all; inserting mid-ladder needs only the tip edited. Rewriting the stack so old snapshots agree is optional tidiness with a real cost. I would write the rule as "the tip is authoritative, prior snapshots are historical" rather than "insertion means a rebase" - otherwise every insertion inherits a rewrite it does not need. For `measure-reproducibility` it is moot: we are rebasing onto `agent-files-model` regardless, so the first occurrence gets the renumber for free.

Two small calls worth making now:

- **1-based.** The old `-0` opening was a phase code; a positional rank starting at zero will generate the same question forever, and TODO ranks are already 1-based. So the opening is `step-1` and the close-out is simply the last step.
- **Frozen at close-out.** Mutability applies to the in-flight ladder only; a chores section's as-built ladder is a record and stops moving once the cycle closes.

**Scope grew.** This now touches five files, not three: `prose.md` (the shape block at :119 and the ladder-step form at :129-131), `cycle.md` (:14-15's "the version suffix encodes the phase", :44-45's version-bump bullet), `versioning.md`, plus `notes.md` and `notes/cycle-protocol.md`, which both codify the as-built ladder form `- [[N]] X.Y.Z[-n] <title>`. Still one commit, just a wider one.

**One acknowledged loss:** done.md could previously be skimmed for 0.24.x vs 0.25.0 to see architecture-vs-increment at a glance. That signal moves entirely into `Cargo.toml` and the log. The reasoning still lives in chores prose, so I would take the trade and note it rather than argue it away.

**The plain version:** agreed, and it makes ladder steps behave exactly like TODO ranks, which is one rule instead of two. Change "insertion means a rebase" to "the tip's TODO.md is authoritative and old snapshots stay as they are" so we do not create rewrites we do not need. Make steps 1-based, freeze a ladder at close-out, and expect the commit to touch five files.

content.text:
Fair, and the project already reached your conclusion once: `custom.md`'s 2026-08-01 entry records that the renumber "would have been free had the cycles run on a topic bookmark landed onto `main` after review". Same reasoning, so the rule is consistent with what we already adopted rather than a new exception.

The framing that makes it precise: **a topic bookmark is a draft until it lands on `main`.** Pushed-to-bookmark is not published. Within the draft, keep the series self-consistent; landing is the moment it becomes history.

Two things that make it safe, both already measured here:

- **`ochid:` trailers survive.** They carry change ids (`/.claude/nrvzusroulsv`), not commit ids, and the 2026-07-31 trapezoid experiment confirmed chids and trailers survived a `jj rebase -s`. So renumbering rungs does not break the cross-repo linkage in either direction.
- **Renumber by amending content, never by re-describing.** Hard rule 4 bans `jj describe` on a trailer-carrying commit; editing `TODO.md` in a rung and amending is not that. Keeping to content-only amendment means self-consistency never needs the rule 4 coordination.

**"When practical" wants named exceptions rather than judgment each time.** I would write three: the bookmark has landed on `main`; another branch is stacked on it (the renumber becomes someone else's rebase); or only a trailing snapshot differs and the ladder is long, where the cost exceeds the inconsistency. Anything else, renumber.

**And a note specific to this branch.** The standard ladder never faces this - `cycle.md:63` says nothing on a ladder is pushed and the close-out squash collapses it, so snapshots evaporate anyway. `measure-reproducibility` is the multi-commit form with rungs pushed individually, which is exactly why it is the first occurrence. So the rule you are stating is really about the trapezoid/pushed-rung shape, and it is worth saying so in the text, otherwise a reader of the squash-form ladder will wonder what problem it solves.

The renumber also implies a bookmark force-push, which stays under hard rule 2 like any other push.

**The plain version:** you are right and the precedent is our own. Write it as "a topic bookmark is a draft until it lands on main; keep the series self-consistent inside it", note the three exceptions so "practical" is not a loophole, and constrain the mechanism to amending content rather than re-describing so the trailer rule stays untouched. Trailers and cross-repo links survive rewrites, so the practice costs a force-push and nothing else.

content.content:
1	# Prose and durable text
2	
3	How long-lived text is written on this project: the prose shape, the punctuation rules, and the
4	commit-title identity. Read this before writing durable text (notes files, commit messages, doc
5	comments, chores sections).
6	
7	Universal file, shared with the template repository; a proposed change is edited here and
8	converges at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
9	Project-local content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).
10	
11	## Prose form
12	
13	Long-lived prose on this project follows one basic shape: a short intro that explains the *why*
14	or the high-level *what*, then a `-` bullet list for the details. Wrap lines at <=100 cols,
15	commit titles and bodies at <=72 (bullet continuations indent two spaces); existing text
16	re-wraps when touched, no mass sweeps. Avoid wall-of-prose paragraphs: they hide the structure
17	that bullets make scannable. Punctuation that joins clauses without naming their relationship is
18	the same failure at sentence scale; see [Semicolons inside bullets](#semicolons-inside-bullets)
19	and [Typeable punctuation only](#typeable-punctuation-only).
20	
21	Surfaces that use this shape:
22	
23	- Module / function / struct / field doc comments in `.rs` files; see
24	  [Doc comments](code.md#doc-comments-on-every-file-function-and-method).
25	- Commit message bodies (both work-repo and bot-repo). The <=72-col title is the
26	  commit-specific add-on; see [Per-commit flow](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow).
27	- Chore descriptions in `notes/chores/chores-NN.md`; see
28	  [Chores section content](notes.md#chores-section-content-no-edit-list-git-is-the-record).
29	- Todo and Done entries in `TODO.md` when an entry needs more than one line of detail. Pure
30	  one-liners are still fine.
31	
32	Bullet *content* differs by surface:
33	
34	- **Commit bodies**: one bullet per *distinct change*, not per file, with detail as sub-bullets
35	  in short sentence fragments (full sentences are discouraged). Source of truth for the
36	  mechanical edit list.
37	  - a file earns its own bullet when its gist is its own: `README.md: new Overview intro`
38	  - files sharing one gist share one bullet, named by common path or glob, and by count once
39	    enumerating stops informing: `agent-data/*.md: "do not edit here" replaced`,
40	    `vendor/: upstream v1.2.3, 1043 files`
41	  - the body is a record, never a directory listing. An import of a thousand files has one
42	    change in it, and restating what `git show --stat` already prints is a second copy that
43	    can drift from the first
44	- **Chores / todo / done**: bullets are conceptual (design points, structural notes, the "what
45	  landed and why" at a notch above file-list granularity). Never a copy of the commit's edit
46	  list; see
47	  [Chores section content](notes.md#chores-section-content-no-edit-list-git-is-the-record).
48	- **Doc comments**: bullets are whatever structure fits (fields, cases, invariants).
49	
50	### Problem + plan shape
51	
52	`## In Progress` cycle blocks, chores section intros, and `## Todo` entries use a sharper form
53	of the same shape:
54	
55	- **Problem statement** (the why): one or two sentences; don't pad with intent, don't restate
56	  the plan.
57	- **Plan bullets** (the what/when): formality differs by surface:
58	  - In Progress / chores: a committed ladder, one step per commit; see
59	    [Conventional-commit shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--chores--commit) for the
60	    per-step title + `(current)` / `(done)` form.
61	  - Todo entries: rough informal bullets, no numbering; formalized only when the entry is
62	    picked up into a cycle.
63	
64	### Semicolons inside bullets
65	
66	A bullet that joins multiple clauses with semicolons (`A; B; C`) is a list hiding inside
67	running prose: break the clauses into sub-bullets so the structure shows. Semicolons in running
68	prose (intro paragraphs, sentence-joins) are fine. Not absolute: very short clauses or tight
69	pairs can stay joined inside a bullet when breaking would be more noise than signal.
70	
71	### Typeable punctuation only
72	
73	Durable text uses punctuation that can be typed at a terminal. Banned: `—`, `–`, `…`, `→`.
74	None can be entered without a compose key or a paste, so none can be grepped for, and an em
75	dash next to option syntax reads as another flag. Unlike the semicolon rule above this one is
76	absolute: they cost nothing to write and are paid on every read, so a soft rule accumulates
77	them.
78	
79	`…` becomes `...` and `→` becomes `->`. The dashes have no single replacement, because an em
80	dash usually stands in for a structural decision that was not made. Make the decision:
81	
82	- **A bullet's title and its body sharing a line** is a heading and a paragraph. Make the body
83	  sub-bullets.
84	- **A term and its definition** (`jj diff`, `<base>`, a flag) takes a colon, which keeps a
85	  glossary or a command list at one line per entry.
86	- **A prose aside** takes a comma, parentheses, or two sentences. Often the aside should just
87	  go.
88	
89	Converting a heading moves its anchor. The em dash strips but the spaces on both sides survive,
90	so `## A — B` slugs to `#a--b` while its colon form slugs to `#a-b` (see
91	[Markdown anchor links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links)). Re-point inbound links in the same
92	commit.
93	
94	Scope is the same as [Speculation marker](#speculation-marker), plus commit titles and
95	everything under `src/`: doc comments, inline comments, and any user-visible string. Source is
96	the surface a human edits and greps most, so an untypeable character costs more there than in
97	prose. It applies going forward; existing text converts when touched. A code span is not exempt
98	by itself. Naming the character is a specimen and stays, which is how this section names them.
99	A banned character doing a job is a use and converts: `` `.expect(…)` `` becomes
100	`` `.expect(...)` ``.
101	
102	Text quoted from outside this repo's prose (tool output, an error message, an already-published
103	commit title) is transcribed, not written, so it keeps its characters, whether or not it sits
104	in a code span. It matters most for commit titles: converting one stops it matching
105	`git log --grep` and breaks the verbatim identity that
106	[Conventional-commit shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--chores--commit) requires between
107	a commit title, its chores header, and its `## Done` entry.
108	
109	### Conventional-commit shape (ladder / chores / commit)
110	
111	A ladder step, its chores section, and its commit description share a *title* shape, a
112	[Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) title (`<type>: <desc>`,
113	an optional `(scope)` after the type: `feat(push): ...`) over [Prose form](#prose-form) detail.
114	They differ in the title's prefix / marker (below) and in bullet *content*: commit bodies are
115	file-by-file, ladder / chores conceptual (see "Bullet *content* differs by surface" above). The
116	shared template:
117	
118	```
119	<optional - X.Y.Z[-N]> <title>   # <title> is the commit's `<type>: <desc>`
120	<optional prose intro>
121	  - <optional item>
122	    <optional prose intro>
123	      - <optional sub-item>
124	      ...
125	```
126	
127	The three surfaces apply it as:
128	
129	- **Ladder step** (`TODO.md` `## In Progress`): the title is prefixed with the version
130	  (`X.Y.Z-N <title>`) and carries a `(current)` / `(done)` marker. The bare three-element
131	  `X.Y.Z` (no `-N`) is the close-out step. Detail is bulleted, never `;`-joined inline.
132	- **Chores section** (`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`): no version prefix, since the `##` header
133	  *is* the bare title, with a `Commits: [[ref]]` line first under it (empty until backfilled;
134	  see [Chores commit references](notes.md#chores-commit-references)).
135	- **Commit description**: no version prefix, and the title is the <=72-col first line; the body
136	  is the prose (file-by-file for the work repo, per
137	  [Per-commit flow](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow)).
138	
139	The title is **identical** across all three for a given step, so a step's ladder entry, its
140	chores `##` header, and its commit title line up verbatim; pick the commit title first and
141	reuse it.
142

# Prose and durable text

How long-lived text is written on this project: the prose shape, the punctuation rules, and the
commit-title identity. Read this before writing durable text (notes files, commit messages, doc
comments, chores sections).

Universal file, shared with the template repository; a proposed change is edited here and
converges at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
Project-local content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).

## Prose form

Long-lived prose on this project follows one basic shape: a short intro that explains the *why*
or the high-level *what*, then a `-` bullet list for the details. Wrap lines at <=100 cols,
commit titles and bodies at <=72 (bullet continuations indent two spaces); existing text
re-wraps when touched, no mass sweeps. Avoid wall-of-prose paragraphs: they hide the structure
that bullets make scannable. Punctuation that joins clauses without naming their relationship is
the same failure at sentence scale; see [Semicolons inside bullets](#semicolons-inside-bullets)
and [Typeable punctuation only](#typeable-punctuation-only).

Surfaces that use this shape:

- Module / function / struct / field doc comments in `.rs` files; see
  [Doc comments](code.md#doc-comments-on-every-file-function-and-method).
- Commit message bodies (both work-repo and bot-repo). The <=72-col title is the
  commit-specific add-on; see [Per-commit flow](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow).
- Chore descriptions in `notes/chores/chores-NN.md`; see
  [Chores section content](notes.md#chores-section-content-no-edit-list-git-is-the-record).
- Todo and Done entries in `TODO.md` when an entry needs more than one line of detail. Pure
  one-liners are still fine.

Bullet *content* differs by surface:

- **Commit bodies**: one bullet per *distinct change*, not per file, with detail as sub-bullets
  in short sentence fragments (full sentences are discouraged). Source of truth for the
  mechanical edit list.
  - a file earns its own bullet when its gist is its own: `README.md: new Overview intro`
  - files sharing one gist share one bullet, named by common path or glob, and by count once
    enumerating stops informing: `agent-data/*.md: "do not edit here" replaced`,
    `vendor/: upstream v1.2.3, 1043 files`
  - the body is a record, never a directory listing. An import of a thousand files has one
    change in it, and restating what `git show --stat` already prints is a second copy that
    can drift from the first
- **Chores / todo / done**: bullets are conceptual (design points, structural notes, the "what
  landed and why" at a notch above file-list granularity). Never a copy of the commit's edit
  list; see
  [Chores section content](notes.md#chores-section-content-no-edit-list-git-is-the-record).
- **Doc comments**: bullets are whatever structure fits (fields, cases, invariants).

### Problem + plan shape

`## In Progress` cycle blocks, chores section intros, and `## Todo` entries use a sharper form
of the same shape:

- **Problem statement** (the why): one or two sentences; don't pad with intent, don't restate
  the plan.
- **Plan bullets** (the what/when): formality differs by surface:
  - In Progress / chores: a committed ladder, one step per commit; see
    [Conventional-commit shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--chores--commit) for the
    per-step title + `(current)` / `(done)` form.
  - Todo entries: rough informal bullets, no numbering; formalized only when the entry is
    picked up into a cycle.

### Semicolons inside bullets

A bullet that joins multiple clauses with semicolons (`A; B; C`) is a list hiding inside
running prose: break the clauses into sub-bullets so the structure shows. Semicolons in running
prose (intro paragraphs, sentence-joins) are fine. Not absolute: very short clauses or tight
pairs can stay joined inside a bullet when breaking would be more noise than signal.

### Typeable punctuation only

Durable text uses punctuation that can be typed at a terminal. Banned: `—`, `–`, `…`, `→`.
None can be entered without a compose key or a paste, so none can be grepped for, and an em
dash next to option syntax reads as another flag. Unlike the semicolon rule above this one is
absolute: they cost nothing to write and are paid on every read, so a soft rule accumulates
them.

`…` becomes `...` and `→` becomes `->`. The dashes have no single replacement, because an em
dash usually stands in for a structural decision that was not made. Make the decision:

- **A bullet's title and its body sharing a line** is a heading and a paragraph. Make the body
  sub-bullets.
- **A term and its definition** (`jj diff`, `<base>`, a flag) takes a colon, which keeps a
  glossary or a command list at one line per entry.
- **A prose aside** takes a comma, parentheses, or two sentences. Often the aside should just
  go.

Converting a heading moves its anchor. The em dash strips but the spaces on both sides survive,
so `## A — B` slugs to `#a--b` while its colon form slugs to `#a-b` (see
[Markdown anchor links](notes.md#markdown-anchor-links)). Re-point inbound links in the same
commit.

Scope is the same as [Speculation marker](#speculation-marker), plus commit titles and
everything under `src/`: doc comments, inline comments, and any user-visible string. Source is
the surface a human edits and greps most, so an untypeable character costs more there than in
prose. It applies going forward; existing text converts when touched. A code span is not exempt
by itself. Naming the character is a specimen and stays, which is how this section names them.
A banned character doing a job is a use and converts: `` `.expect(…)` `` becomes
`` `.expect(...)` ``.

Text quoted from outside this repo's prose (tool output, an error message, an already-published
commit title) is transcribed, not written, so it keeps its characters, whether or not it sits
in a code span. It matters most for commit titles: converting one stops it matching
`git log --grep` and breaks the verbatim identity that
[Conventional-commit shape](#conventional-commit-shape-ladder--chores--commit) requires between
a commit title, its chores header, and its `## Done` entry.

### Conventional-commit shape (ladder / chores / commit)

A ladder step, its chores section, and its commit description share a *title* shape, a
[Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/) title (`<type>: <desc>`,
an optional `(scope)` after the type: `feat(push): ...`) over [Prose form](#prose-form) detail.
They differ in the title's prefix / marker (below) and in bullet *content*: commit bodies are
file-by-file, ladder / chores conceptual (see "Bullet *content* differs by surface" above). The
shared template:

```
<optional - X.Y.Z[-N]> <title>   # <title> is the commit's `<type>: <desc>`
<optional prose intro>
  - <optional item>
    <optional prose intro>
      - <optional sub-item>
      ...
```

The three surfaces apply it as:

- **Ladder step** (`TODO.md` `## In Progress`): the title is prefixed with the version
  (`X.Y.Z-N <title>`) and carries a `(current)` / `(done)` marker. The bare three-element
  `X.Y.Z` (no `-N`) is the close-out step. Detail is bulleted, never `;`-joined inline.
- **Chores section** (`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`): no version prefix, since the `##` header
  *is* the bare title, with a `Commits: [[ref]]` line first under it (empty until backfilled;
  see [Chores commit references](notes.md#chores-commit-references)).
- **Commit description**: no version prefix, and the title is the <=72-col first line; the body
  is the prose (file-by-file for the work repo, per
  [Per-commit flow](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow)).

The title is **identical** across all three for a given step, so a step's ladder entry, its
chores `##` header, and its commit title line up verbatim; pick the commit title first and
reuse it.

That identity is **per step**, not per cycle: each step in a cycle gets its own distinct
descriptive title, never one shared cycle title uniquified by a step marker. The cycle's chores
section header carries the anticipated *close-out* title. To keep a cycle's commits collectable
with one `git log --grep`, give the step titles a common greppable stem (e.g. `config loader`).

## Speculation marker

Durable text the bot writes (agent-files, `notes/`, commit bodies, chores sections)
should stick to observations and direct descriptions of the code or data. If a mechanism,
hypothesis, or causal claim enters the text, prefix it with "We think ..." (a royal "we") so a
reader can tell the measured from the inferred.

**Why:** unmarked speculation reads like evidence, and a future reader (or the bot on a later
session) can pick it up as a known fact when it's not. Measured / inferred is a distinction
worth keeping visible in the written record.

**How to apply:** observations and factual descriptions need no marker. Prefix with
"We think ..." (or a close variant like "Our guess is ...") when the claim is a mechanism
("X wins because Y caches better"), a cause ("the drift was due to thermal state"), a
prediction ("this should scale linearly"), or any reasoning not directly supported by the data
on hand.

## Plain synopsis after technical explanations

When a conversational reply centers on a technical explanation (measurement theory, statistics,
hardware behavior), end it with a short plain-language synopsis, no jargon and no symbols, so
the reader can check their understanding against the technical version.

**Why:** the technical form is precise but easy to misread; the plain form catches
misunderstandings early, when they are cheap.

**How to apply:** conversation only, not notes files (a notes entry should already lead with
the why). Mark it clearly (e.g. "The plain version:"). A reply that is already plain needs no
synopsis.
