# Versioning

How this project versions its commits and the running
artifact. The scheme — the cycle step-numbering and the
unique-per-commit aim — is generic and shared across projects:
this file is copied **verbatim**, with
[Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record)
covering each medium by conditional rather than per-project
edits.

## Terms

Three names, used as defined here across
[AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md),
[cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md), and the notes files:

- **version**: the per-commit version (e.g. `0.3.0-5.3.0`). It lives in the manifest and
  nowhere else. No ladder, chores section, todo entry, commit title, or commit body writes one
  (see
  [Versions live in the version-of-record only](../agent-data/prose.md#versions-live-in-the-version-of-record-only)),
  and its suffix encodes the cycle phase for whoever inspects the manifest (see
  [Step numbering](#step-numbering)).
- **version-of-record** — the authoritative stored copy of the
  version, in the project's manifest (see
  [Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record));
  a built or running artifact derives from it.
- **versioning** — the topic: this scheme as a whole.

## A stamp, not a name

The version answers "which commit produced this artifact". It is not a name for a step: a step is
named by its title and located by its ladder position (see
[Step numbers are positional](../agent-data/prose.md#step-numbers-are-positional)). The two
numberings are therefore free to disagree. Renumbering a ladder does not rewrite the versions
already committed, and it need not, because nothing dereferences a version.

## Recording the version-of-record

Where the version-of-record lives, how it's stored and
surfaced, and how often it changes — pick the case that fits
your medium:

- **Manifest** — where the version-of-record is stored:
  - if Rust, `Cargo.toml` `[package].version`
  - if Python, `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` (or the
    committed config it's sourced from)
  - otherwise wherever the medium records it (a generic
    `version.toml`, a book's frontmatter, …) — add the case as
    needed
- **Notation** — how the `-` form is stored:
  - if the format allows `-` (TOML `version.toml`, `Cargo.toml`),
    store it verbatim
  - if it bars `-` (PEP 440's local segment, e.g. a Python
    project), remap to `+` — `0.3.0-5.3.0` → `0.3.0+5.3.0`: same
    version, just the stored spelling
- **Reporter** — how a built artifact surfaces the
  version-of-record:
  - if a CLI app, `<cli-app> -V`
  - if a TUI/GUI, add to Help/About or display on the title
- **Cadence** — how often to bump: see
  [Unique per commit](#unique-per-commit-preference-not-requirement);
  this project follows the per-commit preference.

## Unique per commit (preference, not requirement)

Our general notion is that the version-of-record should change
on **every commit**, so a built or running artifact identifies
the exact commit it came from.

- This is a preference, **not** a hard requirement. A project
  following the cycle protocol may bump less often — once per
  cycle, only at release, and so on. Record the choice in
  [Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record)
  if it differs.
- It is achievable because the cycle's versions (below) are
  **pre-assignable**, unlike the git SHA, which a commit cannot
  contain (see the cycle protocol's
  [Commits backfill](cycle-protocol.md#commits-backfill)).

## Step numbering

The cycle (Preparation -> Work -> Close-out; see [cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md)) encodes
each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a Preparation**.
This is the manifest's own encoding, for a reader of `Cargo.toml` or of `-V` output; the ladder
names the phase in words instead, and the suffix is not required to match the ladder's step
number:

- `X.Y.Z-0` — Preparation
- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, … — Work commits
- `X.Y.Z` — Close-out (bare version, no suffix)

**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle — no ladder,
no setup commit — skips `-0` and starts at `-1` (its first
Work commit). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that
grows a Preparation later adds the `0` step without
renumbering siblings.

Disambiguation:

- `-10` — Work commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a
  Preparation.
- `-1.0` — Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final
  identifier `0`).

**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:

- `X.Y.Z-3.0` — Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle
- `X.Y.Z-3.1`, `X.Y.Z-3.2` — its Work
- `X.Y.Z-3` — its Close-out
- `X.Y.Z-3.1.0` — Preparation of the `-3.1` sub-sub-cycle

Bump the version-of-record at the start of each phase, so the
active phase is recorded — and, per the preference above,
every commit carries a distinct version.

Ready to commit.

The refinement step is drafted on top of `agent-files-model` as a single-commit cycle, version-of-record 0.24.1 -> 0.24.2. Full validation passed: `cargo fmt` clean, `clippy --all-targets -D warnings` clean, 70 tests pass, `cargo install --locked` replaced 0.24.1 with 0.24.2.

**What the rules now say**

- `AGENTS.md` hard rule 9 gains the load-bearing clause: the title is the only stable identifier, so it must be unique; numbers are positional and versions never appear in prose.
- `agent-data/prose.md` is where the change lives. Two new subsections, `### Step numbers are positional` and `### Versions live in the version-of-record only`, plus the shape template and the three surfaces switched from `X.Y.Z[-N]` to `step-N`, and the commit-body bullet gained the intro rule and "the why and how stay out, they are reachable by construction".
- `agent-data/cycle.md` gets `## Topic bookmarks are drafts`, and per-commit step 6 no longer prescribes a version-bump bullet.
- `agent-data/notes.md`: the as-built rung form is `- [[N]] step-N <title>`, numbers freeze at close-out, and no record carries a version.
- `notes/cycle-protocol.md` (the authority) is re-stated to match: phases named in words, `## Numbering` rewritten, a new `## Topic bookmarks are drafts` with the before/after-landing split and the three exceptions, and `### Body` fixed where it still said one bullet per file.
- `notes/versioning.md` gains `## A stamp, not a name`; the suffix scheme stays as the manifest's own encoding, explicitly not required to match the ladder.

**Three judgment calls to check**

1. **The step number and the version suffix are now separate numberings.** I did not make the suffix literally the step number, because that rewrites versioning.md's `0`-marks-a-Preparation rule, nesting notation and disambiguation cases to buy an agreement nothing reads. Recorded with its residue (someone may expect a rung and a manifest to line up) in a chores subsection, so reversing it is one decision, not an archaeology exercise.
2. **I pulled our project's name back out of `prose.md`.** My first draft cited iiac-perf's 2026-08-01 renumber as the evidence, then I hit our own position recorded a few hundred lines up in chores-06: a pinned file names no project, no project's history, no project's versions. So prose.md states the failure generically and the dated instance lives in `custom.md` where it belongs. Worth knowing this contradicts vc-x1's stated preference (name the member rather than drop the sentence), so it is an open family item, not a settled one.
3. **The two adjacent `## Done` entries still read "the 0.24.0 cycle" / "the 0.24.1 single-commit cycle".** Grandfathering says converts-when-touched and I only appended below them, so I left them. Say the word if you would rather the section be internally consistent now.

Grandfathering is written down for two deliberate keeps: `custom.md`'s renumber mapping (it *is* the decoder, stripping it defeats it) and the previous commit's body with its version-bump bullet (published, and a body is not editable).

file.content:
file-by-file, ladder / chores conceptual (see "Bullet *content* differs by surface" above). The
shared template:

```
<optional - step-N> <title>      # <title> is the commit's `<type>: <desc>`
<optional prose intro>
  - <optional item>
    <optional prose intro>
      - <optional sub-item>
      ...
```

The three surfaces apply it as:

- **Ladder step** (`TODO.md` `## In Progress`): the title is prefixed with the step number
  (`step-N <title>`, 1-based) and carries a `(current)` / `(done)` marker. The last step is the
  close-out and its rung text says so, since nothing in the number does. Detail is bulleted,
  never `;`-joined inline.
- **Chores section** (`notes/chores/chores-NN.md`): no prefix, since the `##` header *is* the
  bare title; the as-built ladder is the first content under it (see
  [Chores commit references](notes.md#chores-commit-references)).
- **Commit description**: no prefix, and the title is the <=72-col first line; the body is the
  prose (see [Commit description](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#commit-description)).

The title is **identical** across all three for a given step, so a step's ladder entry, its
chores `##` header, and its commit title line up verbatim; pick the commit title first and
reuse it.

That identity is **per step**, not per cycle: each step in a cycle gets its own distinct
descriptive title, never one shared cycle title uniquified by a step marker. The cycle's chores
section header carries the anticipated *close-out* title. To keep a cycle's commits collectable
with one `git log --grep`, give the step titles a common greppable stem (e.g. `config loader`).

Because the title is the *only* stable identifier a record has (next section), it must also be
**unique** in the repo's history. A bookend pair stays distinct by construction, since an
opening's title is the close-out's plus one word.

### Step numbers are positional

A ladder's step numbers are position, not identity, exactly like `## Todo` ranks (see
[Todo format](notes.md#todo-format)). They are 1-based, they renumber when a step is inserted,
reordered, or dropped, and nothing refers to a step *by* its number.

- **Titles are the only stable identifiers.** A record points at a step by its title, a plain
  greppable mention, which is why the title is verbatim-identical across the three surfaces and
  unique in the repo's history.
- **The `TODO.md` ladder is authoritative** while the cycle runs. A chores as-built ladder
  records what was built, so it freezes at close-out and stops renumbering even though a live
  ladder does not.
- **Inserting a step renumbers the ladder**, and on an unlanded topic bookmark the rungs that
  already committed the old numbering come along; see
  [Topic bookmarks are drafts](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts).

### Versions live in the version-of-record only

No version appears in durable prose: not in a ladder rung, a chores header or as-built ladder, a
`## Done` entry, `done.md`, a commit title, or a commit body. The manifest is the version's only
written home (see [versioning.md](../notes/versioning.md)), and a commit's version is read from
that file at that commit.

**Why:** the version is a build stamp answering "which commit produced this artifact", not a name
for a step. Written into prose it becomes a second identifier that history is free to invalidate:
one renumber of published versions turns every prose mention, transcript and pasted report into
residue that needs a decoder to read. A renumber cannot touch a title.

**How to apply:** name the step by its title and the phase in words ("the close-out", "the
opening"). Existing versioned prose is grandfathered and converts when touched, no sweep.

## Speculation marker

# Cycle checklists

Checklists for the moments where slips happen: committing, pushing, closing out. The full
protocol, with rationale and recovery procedures, is
[cycle-protocol.md](../notes/cycle-protocol.md); on any disagreement, that file wins. Re-read
the relevant checklist immediately before the action; don't run it from memory.

Universal file, shared with the template repository; a proposed change is edited here and
converges at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
Project-local content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).

## The cycle at a glance

Every change runs as a **cycle**: an optional Preparation step -> Work steps -> a Close-out
step, one commit each. The ladder numbers them `step-1`, `step-2`, ... positionally and names
the phase in words, never in a version; where the version-of-record lives and how often it is
bumped are in [versioning.md](../notes/versioning.md). Read
[cycle-protocol.md](../notes/cycle-protocol.md) before any commit work, and before any push,
cycle or not.

## Committing vs pushing

A cycle rung is committed *by* `vc-x1 push`; never pre-commit it with `jj commit`. Push's
commit stages commit both repos with the approved title/body and stamp each new commit's
`ochid:` trailer (see [ochid trailers](jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)); a
pre-committed rung leaves `@` empty and push mints a stamped empty duplicate (bugs.md #6). In
an instruction, "commit", "push", and "commit + push" all mean `vc-x1 push`. A bare `jj commit`
is asked for by name ("local commit", "just `jj commit`") and is only for work that never
publishes (local-only saves and loop-and-squash intermediates), with no `ochid:`. The approval
around a push, interactive by default and waived only by an explicit scoped delegation, is the
cycle protocol's [Pushing policy](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#policy).

## Topic bookmarks are drafts

A topic bookmark is a draft until it lands on a permanent branch; pushed there is not published.
So keep the series inside it self-consistent: inserting or reordering a step renumbers the
ladder, including the rungs that already committed the old numbering.

- **Amend content, never re-describe.** Editing `TODO.md` in a rung and amending is not a
  `jj describe`, so hard rule 4 stays intact and the `ochid:` trailers ride along untouched
  (they carry change ids, which survive a rewrite).
- **Then force-push the bookmark**, under the same approval as any other push.
- **Exceptions, where self-consistency is not worth its cost**: the bookmark has already landed;
  another branch is stacked on it, so the renumber becomes someone else's rebase; or the ladder
  is long and only a trailing snapshot disagrees.

The squash-form ladder below never meets this, since nothing on it is pushed. The rule is for the
multi-commit shape, whose rungs publish one at a time. Full statement in the protocol's
[Topic bookmarks are drafts](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts).

## Per-commit checklist

Every commit (Preparation, each Work commit, Close-out), per the protocol's
[Per-commit flow](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow):

1. Mark the rung `(current)` in `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, as the first edit.
2. Do the work. On any deviation from the agreed plan, or any question, stop and surface it.
3. Flip `(current)` -> `(done)`, before validation and the commit.
4. Validate the artifact (the medium-specific commands are in [custom.md](../custom.md)).
   Skip-able for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out.
5. Say "ready to commit" and stop. The user reviews the working-copy diff; iterate until
   complete.
6. Write the description: <=72-col conventional title, then a body whose intro names the
   problem this commit resolves and whose bullets record what changed, one per distinct change.
   No version in either, and no why/how (chores, todo, and the session hold those). See
   [Commit description](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#commit-description).
7. Show title + body and stop for review. This review covers the push only when the user's go
   explicitly includes it.
8. On the user's go: `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --title "..." --body "..."`. Never pre-commit with
   `jj commit`; never hand-write `ochid:` trailers.

## Ladder (sub-cycle) checklist

Within a sub-cycle ladder, per the protocol's
[per-Work-commit contract](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#per-work-commit-contract-within-a-ladder):

1. `jj new -R .`: fresh empty `@`.
2. Do the commit's work.
3. Run the fast validation (named in [custom.md](../custom.md)). Non-negotiable.
4. `jj describe -m "..." -m "..." -R .`: scratch working title. This first-time authoring is
   the one permitted describe; the commit is never published and never carries a trailer.

Nothing on a ladder is pushed; the close-out squash
(`jj squash --from "<base>..@-" --into @ -u -R .`) collapses it, and `vc-x1 push` then
publishes the single commit.

## Before any push

- This specific push has the user's explicit approval. Approval of a plan that includes a push
  is not push approval; "commit and push" names the destination, not a waiver of the reviews.
  Only an explicit scoped delegation ("do all of X, don't check in") waives the stops, for that
  bounded task only; destructive ops still pause.
- Validation ran, and passed, after the last edit.
- Closing words are already written; nothing follows the turn's final push (next checklist).

## After the final push: hard stop

Once the turn's final push or bot-repo squash-push is invoked, do no further work: no
verification, no summary, no next-step offers, no edits, until the user speaks. Put all closing
words *before* the invoke. The harness rejects an empty turn, so it may force a visible token
after the tool returns; if so, emit a bare acknowledgment only (e.g. "landed"), never a summary
or more work. Post-push verification happens next turn at the user's direction. A standing
delegation makes intermediate pushes just steps; the hard stop lands on the turn's *final*
push. See
[After push or squash-push](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#after-push-or-squash-push-stop-and-wait).

## Close-out checklist

The cycle's last step, per the protocol's
[Close-out](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#close-out):

1. Move the picked-up item from `## In Progress` to a one-line `## Done` entry with its chores
   `[N]` ref.
2. Finalize the chores section: sync the header to the final commit title (and every anchor
   back-reference), add design subsections; the intro and As-built rungs are already there.
3. Full validation, mandatory.
4. Update `notes/README.md` if functionality changed.
5. At push time, surface the shape options (squash / trapezoid / keep separate) and wait for
   the user's choice. The trapezoid recipe is
   [in the protocol](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#trapezoid-close-out-recipe); its step 4 is
   `jj git push`, not `vc-x1 push`.
6. Backfill the chores as-built ladder refs (and any remaining legacy `Commits:` lines) for
   the commits the previous push made permanent; never record a SHA that is not on a permanent
   branch.

## vc-x1 push behaviors to keep in mind

Three, independent of project language:

- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 assumes nothing about a repo's contents beyond
  `.jj` and `.vc-config.toml`, and runs no build or tests. The medium's validation is the
  per-commit flow's job, run *before* invoking `vc-x1 push`. The one check that remains is
  `push-work` verifying the bookmark's remote refs are tracked, which is its own precondition.
- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume. Every stage no-ops when its
  work is already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If a run fails, push stops and
  reports; getting the repos back to a sensible state is the user's call, not something the
  tool infers.
- **ochid trailers** are injected by `vc-x1 push` itself, so don't hand-write them into the
  commit body or `--title`/`--body`.

## Numbering

The ladder numbers its steps `step-1`, `step-2`, ... in position order, and names each phase in
words. Those numbers are position, not identity: they renumber whenever a step is inserted,
reordered or dropped, and nothing refers to a step by its number. A step is referred to by its
title, which is verbatim-identical in the ladder rung, the chores `##` header and the commit
(see [agent-data/prose.md](../agent-data/prose.md#step-numbers-are-positional)).

The version-of-record still bumps for every step, and its suffix still encodes the phase, but
that encoding is the manifest's own and appears nowhere in prose. Because a renumber does not
rewrite versions already committed, the two numberings may disagree, and nothing breaks when they
do. The full scheme (disambiguation, nesting, optional Preparation, the project's
version-of-record format, and the per-phase bump) lives in
[versioning.md](versioning.md#step-numbering), which is the single source of truth for this
repo's versioning.

## Step numbering

The cycle (Preparation -> Work -> Close-out; see [cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md)) encodes
each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a Preparation**.
This is the manifest's own encoding, for a reader of `Cargo.toml` or of `-V` output; the ladder
names the phase in words instead, and the suffix is not required to match the ladder's step
number:

- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: Work commits
- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)

**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle — no ladder,
no setup commit — skips `-0` and starts at `-1` (its first
Work commit). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that
grows a Preparation later adds the `0` step without
renumbering siblings.

Disambiguation:

- `-10` — Work commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a
  Preparation.
- `-1.0` — Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final
  identifier `0`).

**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:

- `X.Y.Z-3.0` — Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle
- `X.Y.Z-3.1`, `X.Y.Z-3.2` — its Work
- `X.Y.Z-3` — its Close-out
- `X.Y.Z-3.1.0` — Preparation of the `-3.1` sub-sub-cycle

Bump the version-of-record at the start of each phase, so the
active phase is recorded — and, per the preference above,
every commit carries a distinct version.

# Versioning

How this project versions its commits and the running
artifact. The scheme — the cycle step-numbering and the
unique-per-commit aim — is generic and shared across projects:
this file is copied **verbatim**, with
[Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record)
covering each medium by conditional rather than per-project
edits.

## Terms

Three names, used as defined here across
[AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md),
[cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md), and the notes files:

- **version**: the per-commit version (e.g. `0.3.0-5.3.0`). It lives in the manifest and
  nowhere else. No ladder, chores section, todo entry, commit title, or commit body writes one
  (see
  [Versions live in the version-of-record only](../agent-data/prose.md#versions-live-in-the-version-of-record-only)),
  and its suffix encodes the cycle phase for whoever inspects the manifest (see
  [Step numbering](#step-numbering)).
- **version-of-record**: the authoritative stored copy of the version, in the project's manifest
  (see [Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record)); a built or running
  artifact derives from it.
- **versioning**: the topic, this scheme as a whole.

## A stamp, not a name

The version answers "which commit produced this artifact". It is not a name for a step: a step is
named by its title and located by its ladder position (see
[Step numbers are positional](../agent-data/prose.md#step-numbers-are-positional)). The two
numberings are therefore free to disagree. Renumbering a ladder does not rewrite the versions
already committed, and it need not, because nothing dereferences a version.

## Recording the version-of-record

Where the version-of-record lives, how it's stored and
surfaced, and how often it changes — pick the case that fits
your medium:

- **Manifest** — where the version-of-record is stored:
  - if Rust, `Cargo.toml` `[package].version`
  - if Python, `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` (or the
    committed config it's sourced from)
  - otherwise wherever the medium records it (a generic
    `version.toml`, a book's frontmatter, …) — add the case as
    needed
- **Notation** — how the `-` form is stored:
  - if the format allows `-` (TOML `version.toml`, `Cargo.toml`),
    store it verbatim
  - if it bars `-` (PEP 440's local segment, e.g. a Python
    project), remap to `+` — `0.3.0-5.3.0` → `0.3.0+5.3.0`: same
    version, just the stored spelling
- **Reporter** — how a built artifact surfaces the
  version-of-record:
  - if a CLI app, `<cli-app> -V`
  - if a TUI/GUI, add to Help/About or display on the title
- **Cadence** — how often to bump: see
  [Unique per commit](#unique-per-commit-preference-not-requirement);
  this project follows the per-commit preference.

## Unique per commit (preference, not requirement)

Our general notion is that the version-of-record should change
on **every commit**, so a built or running artifact identifies
the exact commit it came from.

- This is a preference, **not** a hard requirement. A project
  following the cycle protocol may bump less often — once per
  cycle, only at release, and so on. Record the choice in
  [Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record)
  if it differs.
- It is achievable because the cycle's versions (below) are
  **pre-assignable**, unlike the git SHA, which a commit cannot
  contain (see the cycle protocol's
  [Commits backfill](cycle-protocol.md#commits-backfill)).

## Step numbering

The cycle (Preparation -> Work -> Close-out; see [cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md)) encodes
each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a Preparation**.
This is the manifest's own encoding, for a reader of `Cargo.toml` or of `-V` output; the ladder
names the phase in words instead, and the suffix is not required to match the ladder's step
number:

- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: Work commits
- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)

**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle — no ladder,
no setup commit — skips `-0` and starts at `-1` (its first
Work commit). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that
grows a Preparation later adds the `0` step without
renumbering siblings.

Disambiguation:

- `-10` — Work commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a
  Preparation.
- `-1.0` — Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final
  identifier `0`).

- `X.Y.Z-3.0` — Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle
- `X.Y.Z-3.1`, `X.Y.Z-3.2` — its Work
- `X.Y.Z-3` — its Close-out
- `X.Y.Z-3.1.0` — Preparation of the `-3.1` sub-sub-cycle

Bump the version-of-record at the start of each phase, so the
active phase is recorded — and, per the preference above,
every commit carries a distinct version.

# Notes

This directory contains various notes and documentation related to the project.
Each file is organized by topic for easy reference.

By default there are the chores-NN.md files in
[chores/](chores). Chores are general notes about tasks;
short term tasks and their status live at the repo root in
[../TODO.md](../TODO.md). The chores-NN files are numbered
in sequence; the highest-numbered file is the active one,
older ones are closed.

Durable design analyses (measurement theory, error models,
decisions that outlive a cycle) live in
[design.md](design.md). Measurement results that outlive a
cycle (e.g. the thread-placement map) live in their own topic
files — [placement-map.md](placement-map.md). Known defects
awaiting a fix live in [bugs.md](bugs.md); durable
machine/session ops facts in [ops.md](ops.md). For users new
to jj see [jj-tips.md](jj-tips.md).

Examples chore file:
```
# Chores-01.md

General maintenance tasks and considerations for the project see other files for
more specific topics. A chore in a chores file provides quick information on the
how and why of a particular chore.

## Create a binary that lists jj info

This binary should list the changeID, commitID, and description title
and using `jj-lib`
```

## Workflow and conventions

Bot-facing workflow and conventions live in
[`../AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md):

- [Notes file conventions](../AGENTS.md#notes-file-conventions)
  — Todo format, Reference numbering, Notes references
  (`[[N]]` citation style), Markdown anchor links, Retiring
  Done entries.
- [Chores conventions](../AGENTS.md#chores-conventions) —
  section headers / Done entries exact-title rule, content
  rules, `Commits:` line format.
- [Code Conventions](../AGENTS.md#code-conventions) — doc
  comments, `// OK: …` on `unwrap*` calls, ask-on-ambiguity,
  stuck detection.

Per-cycle workflow lives in
[`cycle-protocol.md`](cycle-protocol.md):

- [Cycles](cycle-protocol.md#cycles) — three-phase shape
  (Preparation → Work → Close-out), `X.Y.Z-N` numbering,
  sub-cycles.
- [Per-commit flow](cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow) —
  cargo cycle (`fmt` / `clippy` / `test` / `install`),
  work + commit description review gates.
- [Commit description](cycle-protocol.md#commit-description)
  — Conventional Commits, no `(version)` suffix; body shape
  per work vs bot repo.
- [Pushing](cycle-protocol.md#pushing) — push policy,
  close-out shape, `.claude` cadence.

This repo's versioning lives in
[`versioning.md`](versioning.md) — generic and shared
verbatim; the single source of truth that AGENTS.md and
cycle-protocol.md refer to abstractly:

- [Terms](versioning.md#terms) — version / version-of-record /
  versioning.
- [Recording the version-of-record](versioning.md#recording-the-version-of-record)
  — manifest, notation, reporter, and cadence, by medium.
- [Step numbering](versioning.md#step-numbering) — the
  `X.Y.Z-N` scheme, nesting, optional Preparation.

## docs: steps are titles, versions are stamps

- [[N]] docs: steps are titles, versions are stamps

A version written into prose is a second identifier for something that already has one, and it is
the fragile one. This repo proved that on 2026-08-01: renumbering two published versions left
every transcript and pasted report carrying the old banners, and the only thing that can read them
now is a decoder entry in `custom.md`. The titles of those same commits needed nothing. So the
rule inverts. The title is the identifier, the ladder position is how a step is located while it
is in flight, and the version-of-record goes back to being a build stamp that lives in
`Cargo.toml` and nowhere else.

What changed, and why each piece sits where it does:

- **a rung is a bare title.** No version, and no step number either: the rung's place in the
  markdown list already records its place in the ladder, so a number beside it would restate the
  position and then have to be maintained. Inserting or reordering a step edits the list and
  nothing else, which is the whole mechanism
- **the version-of-record still bumps every step**, including a docs-only or agent-file-only one.
  The cadence is unchanged; only its visibility changed. Its suffix is now the single number left
  in the system, it names nothing, and nothing dereferences it
- **titles must be unambiguous, not globally unique**, which is a weaker constraint than the first
  draft of this rule carried. A title is resolved in exactly two places, so those are its scopes:
  within its cycle, so a ladder rung names one step, and within its chores file, since a `##`
  header is also an anchor and GitHub silently resolves a duplicate slug to the first occurrence.
  Across history a title may repeat, and `git log --grep` returning two hits is not a defect
- **commit bodies lose their reasoning.** An intro naming the problem the commit resolves, then the
  mechanical record, and that is all. The dual-repo model is what makes that safe rather than
  lossy: the `ochid:` trailer reaches the session that reasoned the change out, the as-built rung
  reaches this file, and the `## Todo` entry holds the plan. A body that restates them is a second
  copy free to drift from the first
- **a topic bookmark is a draft until it lands.** Keeping its series self-consistent may renumber
  rungs that are already pushed, which is legal because pushing to a bookmark is not publishing.
  The mechanism is content amendment plus a force-push, never a re-describe, so the
  never-re-describe rule and the `ochid:` trailers are both untouched (change ids survive a
  rewrite, as the 2026-07-31 trapezoid experiment measured). Three exceptions are named in the
  protocol so "when practical" is not re-litigated each time

### The step number and the version suffix are now separate numberings

Deliberate, and the alternative was weighed: the version suffix could have *become* the step
number, one numbering serving both. That was rejected because it rewrites `versioning.md`'s scheme
(the final-`0`-marks-a-Preparation rule, the nesting notation, the disambiguation cases) to buy an
agreement that nothing reads. Two numberings that never appear side by side cannot be confused for
each other, and the suffix keeps doing its one job: telling a reader of `-V` output which phase a
build came from.

The residue is a single latent trap, that someone comparing a rung to a manifest may expect the
numbers to line up. `versioning.md` now says they need not, which is the cheapest fix available.

### Grandfathering, and what deliberately keeps its versions

Versioned prose already in the repo is not swept; it converts when its surrounding text is
touched, the same treatment the legacy `Commits:` lines got. Two cases are deliberate rather than
pending:

- **`custom.md`'s 2026-08-01 renumber entry keeps its version mapping.** It *is* the decoder for
  the residue, so stripping the versions out of it would defeat its purpose.
- **the previous commit's body keeps its version-bump bullet.** It is published on this bookmark
  and a body is not editable text; the rule applies from here forward rather than backwards.

### Drafted before the rebase, on purpose

The step lands on `agent-files-model` ahead of rebasing `measure-reproducibility` onto it, so the
next cycle runs its ladder under these rules and the family reply carries evidence instead of
intent. Refinements the dogfood turns up are collected in `TODO.md` and land as a later batch
step, rather than each one triggering another rebase of the in-flight rungs.

# References

  the number was restating the list position and adding a maintenance obligation, and the
  renumber-on-insert rule the second pass needed was work invented by the first pass. What
  survives is the part that was doing the job: the title.

renderer step" instead of "step-3", which is longer to say and cannot be ambiguous inside one
cycle. The residue is that `versioning.md`'s suffix is the last number standing, and it is now
explicit there that it names nothing.

# Cycle checklists

Checklists for the moments where slips happen: committing, pushing, closing out. The full
protocol, with rationale and recovery procedures, is
[cycle-protocol.md](../notes/cycle-protocol.md); on any disagreement, that file wins. Re-read

converges at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
Project-local content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).

## The cycle at a glance

Every change runs as a **cycle**: an optional Preparation step -> Work steps -> a Close-out
step, one commit each. The ladder lists them in order and identifies each by its title, with no
number and no version; where the version-of-record lives and how often it is bumped are in
[versioning.md](../notes/versioning.md). Read
[cycle-protocol.md](../notes/cycle-protocol.md) before any commit work, and before any push,
cycle or not.

## Committing vs pushing

A cycle rung is committed *by* `vc-x1 push`; never pre-commit it with `jj commit`. Push's
commit stages commit both repos with the approved title/body and stamp each new commit's
`ochid:` trailer (see [ochid trailers](jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)); a
pre-committed rung leaves `@` empty and push mints a stamped empty duplicate (bugs.md #6). In
an instruction, "commit", "push", and "commit + push" all mean `vc-x1 push`. A bare `jj commit`
is asked for by name ("local commit", "just `jj commit`") and is only for work that never
publishes (local-only saves and loop-and-squash intermediates), with no `ochid:`. The approval
around a push, interactive by default and waived only by an explicit scoped delegation, is the
cycle protocol's [Pushing policy](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#policy).

## Topic bookmarks are drafts

A topic bookmark is a draft until it lands on a permanent branch; pushed there is not published.
So keep the series inside it self-consistent: inserting or reordering a step edits the ladder in
the rungs that already committed an older version of it, not only at the tip.

- **Amend content, never re-describe.** Editing `TODO.md` in a rung and amending is not a
  `jj describe`, so hard rule 4 stays intact and the `ochid:` trailers ride along untouched
  (they carry change ids, which survive a rewrite).
- **Then force-push the bookmark**, under the same approval as any other push.
- **Exceptions, where self-consistency is not worth its cost**: the bookmark has already landed;
  another branch is stacked on it, so the renumber becomes someone else's rebase; or the ladder
  is long and only a trailing snapshot disagrees.

The squash-form ladder below never meets this, since nothing on it is pushed. The rule is for the
multi-commit shape, whose rungs publish one at a time. Full statement in the protocol's
[Topic bookmarks are drafts](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts).

## Per-commit checklist

Every commit (Preparation, each Work commit, Close-out), per the protocol's
[Per-commit flow](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow):

1. Mark the rung `(current)` in `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, as the first edit.
2. Do the work. On any deviation from the agreed plan, or any question, stop and surface it.
3. Flip `(current)` -> `(done)`, before validation and the commit.
4. Validate the artifact (the medium-specific commands are in [custom.md](../custom.md)).
   Skip-able for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out.
5. Say "ready to commit" and stop. The user reviews the working-copy diff; iterate until
   complete.
6. Write the description: <=72-col conventional title, then a body whose intro names the
   problem this commit resolves and whose bullets record what changed, one per distinct change.
   No version in either, and no why/how (chores, todo, and the session hold those). See
   [Commit description](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#commit-description).
7. Show title + body and stop for review. This review covers the push only when the user's go
   explicitly includes it.
8. On the user's go: `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --title "..." --body "..."`. Never pre-commit with
   `jj commit`; never hand-write `ochid:` trailers.

## Ladder (sub-cycle) checklist

Within a sub-cycle ladder, per the protocol's
[per-Work-commit contract](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#per-work-commit-contract-within-a-ladder):

1. `jj new -R .`: fresh empty `@`.
2. Do the commit's work.
3. Run the fast validation (named in [custom.md](../custom.md)). Non-negotiable.
4. `jj describe -m "..." -m "..." -R .`: scratch working title. This first-time authoring is
   the one permitted describe; the commit is never published and never carries a trailer.

Nothing on a ladder is pushed; the close-out squash
(`jj squash --from "<base>..@-" --into @ -u -R .`) collapses it, and `vc-x1 push` then
publishes the single commit.

## Before any push

- This specific push has the user's explicit approval. Approval of a plan that includes a push
  is not push approval; "commit and push" names the destination, not a waiver of the reviews.
  Only an explicit scoped delegation ("do all of X, don't check in") waives the stops, for that
  bounded task only; destructive ops still pause.
- Validation ran, and passed, after the last edit.
- Closing words are already written; nothing follows the turn's final push (next checklist).

## After the final push: hard stop

Once the turn's final push or bot-repo squash-push is invoked, do no further work: no
verification, no summary, no next-step offers, no edits, until the user speaks. Put all closing
words *before* the invoke. The harness rejects an empty turn, so it may force a visible token
after the tool returns; if so, emit a bare acknowledgment only (e.g. "landed"), never a summary
or more work. Post-push verification happens next turn at the user's direction. A standing
delegation makes intermediate pushes just steps; the hard stop lands on the turn's *final*
push. See
[After push or squash-push](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#after-push-or-squash-push-stop-and-wait).

## Close-out checklist

The cycle's last step, per the protocol's
[Close-out](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#close-out):

1. Move the picked-up item from `## In Progress` to a one-line `## Done` entry with its chores
   `[N]` ref.
2. Finalize the chores section: sync the header to the final commit title (and every anchor
   back-reference), add design subsections; the intro and As-built rungs are already there.
3. Full validation, mandatory.
4. Update `notes/README.md` if functionality changed.
5. At push time, surface the shape options (squash / trapezoid / keep separate) and wait for
   the user's choice. The trapezoid recipe is
   [in the protocol](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#trapezoid-close-out-recipe); its step 4 is
   `jj git push`, not `vc-x1 push`.
6. Backfill the chores as-built ladder refs (and any remaining legacy `Commits:` lines) for
   the commits the previous push made permanent; never record a SHA that is not on a permanent
   branch.

## vc-x1 push behaviors to keep in mind

Three, independent of project language:

- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 assumes nothing about a repo's contents beyond
  `.jj` and `.vc-config.toml`, and runs no build or tests. The medium's validation is the
  per-commit flow's job, run *before* invoking `vc-x1 push`. The one check that remains is
  `push-work` verifying the bookmark's remote refs are tracked, which is its own precondition.
- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume. Every stage no-ops when its
  work is already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If a run fails, push stops and
  reports; getting the repos back to a sensible state is the user's call, not something the
  tool infers.
- **ochid trailers** are injected by `vc-x1 push` itself, so don't hand-write them into the
  commit body or `--title`/`--body`.

# Notes

This directory contains various notes and documentation related to the project.
Each file is organized by topic for easy reference.

By default there are the chores-NN.md files in
[chores/](chores). Chores are general notes about tasks;
short term tasks and their status live at the repo root in
[../TODO.md](../TODO.md). The chores-NN files are numbered
in sequence; the highest-numbered file is the active one,
older ones are closed.

Durable design analyses (measurement theory, error models,
decisions that outlive a cycle) live in
[design.md](design.md). Measurement results that outlive a
cycle (e.g. the thread-placement map) live in their own topic
files — [placement-map.md](placement-map.md). Known defects
awaiting a fix live in [bugs.md](bugs.md); durable
machine/session ops facts in [ops.md](ops.md). For users new
to jj see [jj-tips.md](jj-tips.md).

```
# Chores-01.md

General maintenance tasks and considerations for the project see other files for
more specific topics. A chore in a chores file provides quick information on the
how and why of a particular chore.

## Create a binary that lists jj info

This binary should list the changeID, commitID, and description title
and using `jj-lib`
```

[`../AGENTS.md`](../AGENTS.md):

  Done entries.

  comments, `// OK: …` on `unwrap*` calls, ask-on-ambiguity,
  stuck detection.

Per-cycle workflow lives in
[`cycle-protocol.md`](cycle-protocol.md):

- [Cycles](cycle-protocol.md#cycles) — three-phase shape

  sub-cycles.
- [Per-commit flow](cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow) —
  cargo cycle (`fmt` / `clippy` / `test` / `install`),
  work + commit description review gates.
- [Commit description](cycle-protocol.md#commit-description)
  — Conventional Commits, no `(version)` suffix; body shape
  per work vs bot repo.
- [Pushing](cycle-protocol.md#pushing) — push policy,
  close-out shape, `.claude` cadence.

This repo's versioning lives in
[`versioning.md`](versioning.md) — generic and shared
verbatim; the single source of truth that AGENTS.md and
cycle-protocol.md refer to abstractly:

- [Terms](versioning.md#terms) — version / version-of-record /

- [Recording the version-of-record](versioning.md#recording-the-version-of-record)

- [Suffix scheme](versioning.md#suffix-scheme): the manifest's `X.Y.Z-N` spelling, nesting,
  optional Preparation.

content.text:
Thoughts only, no edits.

**My answer is no**, and one argument decides it: it re-couples the version to the title, in the direction that fires more often.

The case for titles was that history can invalidate a version but cannot touch a title. Embed the slug in the version and that inverts: a *retitle* now invalidates every version string ever stamped. And retitles are common by our own rules. `notes.md` says a commit-recording header is provisional while the work is in progress and the last edit before push syncs it to the final title; `cycle.md` step 2 of close-out syncs the header if the cycle's scope shifted. So the mutable thing would be feeding the immutable thing. We would have traded rare renumber-residue for frequent retitle-residue.

**The steelman deserves saying, because it is strong.** This project's actual residue problem is pasted report banners nobody can decode weeks later, which is exactly what `custom.md`'s decoder entry exists for. A banner reading `iiac-perf 0.25.0-warm-until-the-window-grades-a` is self-decoding; `0.25.0-2` is not. That is a real gain and it lands precisely where this project bleeds.

The counter is a clean trade to state: **slugs buy usually-self-decoding at the price of sometimes-undecodable; numbers are never-self-decoding but always-decodable.** A slug whose step was later retitled greps to nothing, while a number plus the manifest's history always resolves. For a harness whose reports outlive their context, I would rather have the always-decodable one.

**Costs beyond that, briefly:**

- **Semver ordering goes.** Prerelease identifiers compare ASCII-alphabetically, so `-docs-x` sorts before `-refactor-y` for no reason related to step order. Two binaries in hand stop telling you which is later. Bare close-out still outranks all prereleases, so only within-cycle ordering breaks, but that is the ordering we look at most.
- **It is not a 3-line edit.** Lines 90-92 are the surface; the section's grammar underneath is the final-`0`-marks-a-Preparation rule, the `-10` vs `-1.0` disambiguation, and the recursive nesting. Slugs delete all of it. That is the same cost that killed "make the suffix be the step number" two passes ago, for less benefit.
- **Banner width.** ~35 extra characters in `-V`, in `cargo install` output, and in the report header, on an artifact whose reports are already dense and column-aligned. Worth checking whether `qualify.rs` parses anything off the banner line before assuming this is only cosmetic.

**If the goal is the steelman, there is a way to get it without the coupling:** bake the commit title (or `git describe`) into the binary as build metadata and print it beside the version. The title stays the single source of truth instead of being copied into a field that cannot be edited, semver keeps ordering, and the banner becomes self-decoding. Semver's `+` build metadata is the in-version version of the same idea and is explicitly ignored for ordering, but it still copies the title, so I prefer the separate field.

**Sequencing, either way:** not a fold-in. The current step is validated and internally consistent; this would re-open versioning.md's grammar, the report banner, and possibly a parser. It is its own cycle, and a good candidate to decide *after* the dogfood, when we know whether we actually miss the legibility.

**The plain version:** it is a tempting idea because our real pain is undecodable banners in pasted reports, and a title in the version would fix that. But it makes the version depend on the title, and titles get edited, so the fragility comes back pointed the other way. It also costs the ability to tell which of two builds is newer. If we want a running binary to say in words where it came from, print the commit title next to the version rather than inside it, and take that up as its own cycle after the dogfood.

Correct, and as drafted they are stronger than a recommendation. Both are flat rules, in the same register as the typeable-punctuation rule rather than the semicolon one.

Where you will find them while reading:

- `AGENTS.md` rule 9: "The title is a step's only identifier, so it carries no number and no version."
- `agent-data/prose.md` `### Steps are named, not numbered`: "A step has a title and no number. Nothing in a ladder rung, a chores as-built rung, a `## Done` entry, or a commit gives a step an ordinal."
- `agent-data/prose.md` `### Versions live in the version-of-record only`: "No version appears in durable prose: not in a ladder rung, a chores header or as-built ladder, a `## Done` entry, `done.md`, a commit title, or a commit body."
- `notes/cycle-protocol.md` `## Step naming` and `## Commit description`: "**A commit names no version**, in its title or its body."

**The step-number half is now enforced by construction, not by discipline.** Nothing in the system generates a step number any more, so there is no habit to resist. The only numbers left are `## Todo` ranks, named as the deliberate exception because a priority list has an order worth reading off, and the manifest suffix, which no prose surface touches.

Three exceptions exist on purpose, and each has to name itself: grandfathering (existing versioned prose converts when touched, no sweep), `custom.md`'s 2026-08-01 renumber mapping, which *is* the decoder and would be defeated by stripping it, and the previous commit's body, which is already published. An exception that must state its reason is auditable in a way a strong recommendation is not, which is why I would keep the absolute framing rather than soften it.

**One gap I would close, and it is the only substantive thing I would add.** `prose.md`'s punctuation rule already carries the distinction this needs: "Naming the character is a specimen and stays ... A banned character doing a job is a use and converts." The version rule has no such sentence, and it needs one, because legitimate prose *about* versioning names versions constantly: `versioning.md`'s own `X.Y.Z-N` grammar, `custom.md`'s "minor for architecture, patch for everything else", the decoder mapping, a chores narrative describing a renumber. Those are specimens. A version standing in for a step's name is a use. Without that line drawn, the rule either reads as violated by its own documentation or invites an argument each time.

**Scope note, deliberate:** the rule covers durable text, not conversation. We will keep saying "install 0.24.2" out loud, and should. The old wording in `versioning.md` extended to "commit talk"; the replacement does not, which I take as an improvement rather than an oversight, but flag it in case you meant it to bind talk too.

**The plain version:** yes, and they are hard rules rather than recommendations, with three exceptions that each say why. The one thing missing is a sentence saying that writing *about* versions is fine while using a version *as a step's name* is not, copied in spirit from how the punctuation rule separates naming a character from using one. Say the word after your read and I will add it.

Your miss is the useful part of this: **the version was doing a second job nobody credited it with — a short, high-contrast landmark per entry.** We removed it on identity grounds and got a legibility regression. That is exactly the kind of finding the dogfood is supposed to produce, and it should land in the chores narrative and the `custom.md` entry whichever way we fix it, because vc-x1 will hit it too.

**But I would not restore the version as the anchor, because it was a weak one.** You scanned for `0.24.2`, did not find it, and concluded the entry was missing. The landmark told you nothing about what was there; it only reported that a number you predicted was absent. A title anchor answers the question you actually had. So the fix is not to bring back a weak landmark, it is to make the strong one visible.

**The real defect is older than this change, and our own files already say so.** Two rules still specify a one-liner: `notes.md`'s migration step ("a one-line `## Done` entry with its chores `[N]` ref") and cycle-protocol's Close-out ("a one-line entry (with a chores `[N]` ref)"). Reality drifted to five- and six-line paragraphs, and `prose.md` quietly blessed the drift ("Todo and Done entries ... when an entry needs more than one line of detail") while its own Prose form warns that wall-of-prose paragraphs "hide the structure that bullets make scannable". So `## Done` has been violating prose.md for a while; the version was masking it.

**Three ways out, and my lean:**

1. **Title line, detail as sub-bullets.** This is just Prose form applied to a surface that was exempting itself, so it needs no new rule, only the removal of the "one-line" wording that nobody follows. Uniform across `TODO.md` and `done.md`, so the migration step still moves a bullet verbatim.
2. **Enforce the actual one-liner**, on the argument that a Done entry is a pointer and every word past that duplicates the chores intro, which is the same second-copy-drifts argument prose.md already makes for commit bodies. Cleanest and most scannable, but it turns `done.md` into a table of contents, and there is real value in that file reading as "what this project has shipped" standalone.
3. **Bold the title** and keep the paragraph. Cheapest, and it matches cycle-protocol's Preparation step, which already specifies "a **bold title line**" for `## In Progress`.

I would take 1, with the bolding from 3 as a free add-on, and I would not take 2 despite liking its logic, because `done.md` is the only narrative record of the project's arc and shrinking it to refs costs more than the scan gains.

**Scope, if we do it now:** fix the two "one-line" sentences, fix prose.md's blessing of the paragraph form, and reformat the three live entries in `TODO.md`. `done.md`'s ~100 existing entries stay as they are under grandfathering, converting when touched. That is small enough to fold into this step, and I would rather fold it than ship a rule that visibly regresses the file it governs and fix it next cycle.

**One bound worth noting:** this regression is specific to Done and done.md entries, the only surface where a long body hangs off a title in a flat list. Chores as-built ladders got *more* scannable (rungs are one short line each and lost a token), and `## Todo` keeps its ranks. So the fix does not spread.

**The plain version:** you were using the version number as a place to rest your eye, and taking it away made a list of long paragraphs harder to skim. The answer is not to put the number back, since it was a poor landmark that only told you a number was missing. Give each Done entry a title line with its detail as sub-bullets, optionally bold the title, and fix the two rules that still claim these entries are one line long. Small enough to include in this step, and the regression itself is worth recording as evidence for the family.

## Done entry form

A `## Done` entry (in `TODO.md` and in `done.md`) is a **bold title line** carrying its chores
`[[N]]` ref, with any detail as sub-bullets:

```
- **feat: config loader** [[7]]
  - `--config` resolves per-profile pin pools
  - the parse rejects unknown keys rather than ignoring them
```

- **Bold, and detail below rather than beside.** These entries are read by skimming a list for
  one of them, so the title has to be findable without reading the line it sits on. A title
  followed by a paragraph of summary is the wall-of-prose shape
  [Prose form](prose.md#prose-form) warns about, and it hides the one thing a skim is looking
  for. Bold matches the `## In Progress` block, whose title line is already bold.
- **A one-liner is still fine** when the title says it all; the sub-bullets are for when it does
  not. What is not fine is the middle case, a title with sentences trailing off it.
- **Sub-bullets are conceptual, like chores bullets**: what shipped, not a file list, and never
  a copy of the chores intro. The `[[N]]` ref is what carries a reader to the full narrative.

# Cycle checklists

Checklists for the moments where slips happen: committing, pushing, closing out. The full
protocol, with rationale and recovery procedures, is
[cycle-protocol.md](../notes/cycle-protocol.md); on any disagreement, that file wins. Re-read
the relevant checklist immediately before the action; don't run it from memory.

Universal file, shared with the template repository; a proposed change is edited here and
converges at the template ([Changing the agent-files](../AGENTS.md#changing-the-agent-files)).
Project-local content goes in [custom.md](../custom.md).

## The cycle at a glance

Every change runs as a **cycle**: an optional Preparation step -> Work steps -> a Close-out
step, one commit each. The ladder lists them in order and identifies each by its title, with no
number and no version; where the version-of-record lives and how often it is bumped are in
[versioning.md](../notes/versioning.md). Read
[cycle-protocol.md](../notes/cycle-protocol.md) before any commit work, and before any push,
cycle or not.

## Committing vs pushing

A cycle rung is committed *by* `vc-x1 push`; never pre-commit it with `jj commit`. Push's
commit stages commit both repos with the approved title/body and stamp each new commit's
`ochid:` trailer (see [ochid trailers](jj.md#cross-repo-linking-ochid-trailers)); a
pre-committed rung leaves `@` empty and push mints a stamped empty duplicate (bugs.md #6). In
an instruction, "commit", "push", and "commit + push" all mean `vc-x1 push`. A bare `jj commit`
is asked for by name ("local commit", "just `jj commit`") and is only for work that never
publishes (local-only saves and loop-and-squash intermediates), with no `ochid:`. The approval
around a push, interactive by default and waived only by an explicit scoped delegation, is the
cycle protocol's [Pushing policy](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#policy).

## Topic bookmarks are drafts

A topic bookmark is a draft until it lands on a permanent branch; pushed there is not published.
So keep the series inside it self-consistent: inserting or reordering a step edits the ladder in
the rungs that already committed an older version of it, not only at the tip.

- **Amend content, never re-describe.** Editing `TODO.md` in a rung and amending is not a
  `jj describe`, so hard rule 4 stays intact and the `ochid:` trailers ride along untouched
  (they carry change ids, which survive a rewrite).
- **Then force-push the bookmark**, under the same approval as any other push.
- **Exceptions, where self-consistency is not worth its cost**: the bookmark has already landed;
  another branch is stacked on it, so the rewrite becomes someone else's rebase; or the ladder
  is long and only a trailing snapshot disagrees.

The squash-form ladder below never meets this, since nothing on it is pushed. The rule is for the
multi-commit shape, whose rungs publish one at a time. Full statement in the protocol's
[Topic bookmarks are drafts](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#topic-bookmarks-are-drafts).

## Per-commit checklist

Every commit (Preparation, each Work commit, Close-out), per the protocol's
[Per-commit flow](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#per-commit-flow):

1. Mark the rung `(current)` in `TODO.md > ## In Progress`, as the first edit.
2. Do the work. On any deviation from the agreed plan, or any question, stop and surface it.
3. Flip `(current)` -> `(done)`, before validation and the commit.
4. Validate the artifact (the medium-specific commands are in [custom.md](../custom.md)).
   Skip-able for notes-only commits, mandatory at close-out.
5. Say "ready to commit" and stop. The user reviews the working-copy diff; iterate until
   complete.
6. Write the description: <=72-col conventional title, then a body whose intro names the
   problem this commit resolves and whose bullets record what changed, one per distinct change.
   No version in either, and no why/how (chores, todo, and the session hold those). See
   [Commit description](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#commit-description).
7. Show title + body and stop for review. This review covers the push only when the user's go
   explicitly includes it.
8. On the user's go: `vc-x1 push <bookmark> --title "..." --body "..."`. Never pre-commit with
   `jj commit`; never hand-write `ochid:` trailers.

## Ladder (sub-cycle) checklist

Within a sub-cycle ladder, per the protocol's
[per-Work-commit contract](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#per-work-commit-contract-within-a-ladder):

1. `jj new -R .`: fresh empty `@`.
2. Do the commit's work.
3. Run the fast validation (named in [custom.md](../custom.md)). Non-negotiable.
4. `jj describe -m "..." -m "..." -R .`: scratch working title. This first-time authoring is
   the one permitted describe; the commit is never published and never carries a trailer.

Nothing on a ladder is pushed; the close-out squash
(`jj squash --from "<base>..@-" --into @ -u -R .`) collapses it, and `vc-x1 push` then
publishes the single commit.

## Before any push

- This specific push has the user's explicit approval. Approval of a plan that includes a push
  is not push approval; "commit and push" names the destination, not a waiver of the reviews.
  Only an explicit scoped delegation ("do all of X, don't check in") waives the stops, for that
  bounded task only; destructive ops still pause.
- Validation ran, and passed, after the last edit.
- Closing words are already written; nothing follows the turn's final push (next checklist).

## After the final push: hard stop

Once the turn's final push or bot-repo squash-push is invoked, do no further work: no
verification, no summary, no next-step offers, no edits, until the user speaks. Put all closing
words *before* the invoke. The harness rejects an empty turn, so it may force a visible token
after the tool returns; if so, emit a bare acknowledgment only (e.g. "landed"), never a summary
or more work. Post-push verification happens next turn at the user's direction. A standing
delegation makes intermediate pushes just steps; the hard stop lands on the turn's *final*
push. See
[After push or squash-push](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#after-push-or-squash-push-stop-and-wait).

## Close-out checklist

The cycle's last step, per the protocol's
[Close-out](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#close-out):

1. Move the picked-up item from `## In Progress` to a one-line `## Done` entry with its chores
   `[N]` ref.
2. Finalize the chores section: sync the header to the final commit title (and every anchor
   back-reference), add design subsections; the intro and As-built rungs are already there.
3. Full validation, mandatory.
4. Update `notes/README.md` if functionality changed.
5. At push time, surface the shape options (squash / trapezoid / keep separate) and wait for
   the user's choice. The trapezoid recipe is
   [in the protocol](../notes/cycle-protocol.md#trapezoid-close-out-recipe); its step 4 is
   `jj git push`, not `vc-x1 push`.
6. Backfill the chores as-built ladder refs (and any remaining legacy `Commits:` lines) for
   the commits the previous push made permanent; never record a SHA that is not on a permanent
   branch.

## vc-x1 push behaviors to keep in mind

Three, independent of project language:

- **No checks of the project's own.** vc-x1 assumes nothing about a repo's contents beyond
  `.jj` and `.vc-config.toml`, and runs no build or tests. The medium's validation is the
  per-commit flow's job, run *before* invoking `vc-x1 push`. The one check that remains is
  `push-work` verifying the bookmark's remote refs are tracked, which is its own precondition.
- **Rerunning is safe.** Push keeps no state and cannot resume. Every stage no-ops when its
  work is already done, so a failed run is re-run, not resumed. If a run fails, push stops and
  reports; getting the repos back to a sensible state is the user's call, not something the
  tool infers.
- **ochid trailers** are injected by `vc-x1 push` itself, so don't hand-write them into the
  commit body or `--title`/`--body`.

### The version was also a landmark, which is how the Done entries got reshaped

Found by wink reading this very step: scanning `TODO.md > ## Done` for the new entry meant looking
for `0.24.2`, not finding it, and concluding the entry was missing. It was there. The version had
been doing a second job nobody had credited it with, a short high-contrast token per entry that
the eye could rest on, and removing it exposed what it had been masking.

The fix is not to restore it, because it was a poor landmark: its absence reported that a predicted
number was missing, not that an entry was. A title answers the question a skim is actually asking.
So the entries changed shape instead.

- **A `## Done` entry is now a bold title line plus sub-bullets** (`agent-data/notes.md`
  [Done entry form](../../agent-data/notes.md#done-entry-form)), matching the `## In Progress`
  block, whose title line was already bold.
- **The old form violated `prose.md` and had done so for a while.** A title with five lines of
  summary trailing off it is the wall-of-prose shape Prose form warns about, and two rules still
  called these entries one-liners (`notes.md`'s migration step and cycle-protocol's Close-out)
  while `prose.md` separately blessed the paragraph. The version was hiding a drift, not
  preventing one; all three now agree.
- **The three live entries were converted**, versions dropped from the two older ones too, at
  wink's call, so the section can be judged in its new form rather than in a mixture. `done.md`'s
  existing entries stay under grandfathering.

Bounded on purpose: Done and `done.md` entries are the only surface where a long body hangs off a
title in a flat list. Chores as-built ladders got *more* skimmable, since a rung is one short line
that lost a token, and `## Todo` keeps its ranks.

# Versioning

How this project versions its commits and the running
artifact. The scheme — the cycle step-numbering and the
unique-per-commit aim — is generic and shared across projects:
this file is copied **verbatim**, with
[Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record)
covering each medium by conditional rather than per-project
edits.

## Terms

Three names, used as defined here across
[AGENTS.md](../AGENTS.md),
[cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md), and the notes files:

- **version**: the per-commit version (e.g. `0.3.0-5.3.0`). It lives in the manifest and
  nowhere else. No ladder, chores section, todo entry, commit title, or commit body writes one
  (see
  [Versions live in the version-of-record only](../agent-data/prose.md#versions-live-in-the-version-of-record-only)),
  and its suffix encodes the cycle phase for whoever inspects the manifest (see
  [Suffix scheme](#suffix-scheme)).
- **version-of-record**: the authoritative stored copy of the version, in the project's manifest
  (see [Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record)); a built or running
  artifact derives from it.
- **versioning**: the topic, this scheme as a whole.

## A stamp, not a name

The version answers "which commit produced this artifact". It is not a name for a step: a step is
named by its title and located by its position in the ladder list (see
[Steps are named, not numbered](../agent-data/prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)). So the
suffix below is the only number in the system, and since nothing dereferences it, reordering or
inserting a step leaves the versions already committed alone.

## Recording the version-of-record

Where the version-of-record lives, how it's stored and
surfaced, and how often it changes — pick the case that fits
your medium:

- **Manifest** — where the version-of-record is stored:
  - if Rust, `Cargo.toml` `[package].version`
  - if Python, `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` (or the
    committed config it's sourced from)
  - otherwise wherever the medium records it (a generic
    `version.toml`, a book's frontmatter, …) — add the case as
    needed
- **Notation** — how the `-` form is stored:
  - if the format allows `-` (TOML `version.toml`, `Cargo.toml`),
    store it verbatim
  - if it bars `-` (PEP 440's local segment, e.g. a Python
    project), remap to `+` — `0.3.0-5.3.0` → `0.3.0+5.3.0`: same
    version, just the stored spelling
- **Reporter** — how a built artifact surfaces the
  version-of-record:
  - if a CLI app, `<cli-app> -V`
  - if a TUI/GUI, add to Help/About or display on the title
- **Cadence** — how often to bump: see
  [Unique per commit](#unique-per-commit-preference-not-requirement);
  this project follows the per-commit preference.

## Unique per commit (preference, not requirement)

Our general notion is that the version-of-record should change
on **every commit**, so a built or running artifact identifies
the exact commit it came from.

- This is a preference, **not** a hard requirement. A project
  following the cycle protocol may bump less often — once per
  cycle, only at release, and so on. Record the choice in
  [Recording the version-of-record](#recording-the-version-of-record)
  if it differs.
- It is achievable because the cycle's versions (below) are
  **pre-assignable**, unlike the git SHA, which a commit cannot
  contain (see the cycle protocol's
  [Commits backfill](cycle-protocol.md#commits-backfill)).

## Suffix scheme

The cycle (Preparation -> Work -> Close-out; see [cycle-protocol.md](cycle-protocol.md)) encodes
each commit's phase in the version suffix, the **final identifier `0` marking a Preparation**.

This is the manifest's own spelling, read by whoever inspects `Cargo.toml` or `-V` output. It is
not a name for a step and it is not written anywhere else: a step is identified by its title, and
a ladder rung carries neither a number nor a version (see
[Steps are named, not numbered](../agent-data/prose.md#steps-are-named-not-numbered)). The
identifiers below therefore count commits within a phase; nothing dereferences one.

- `X.Y.Z-0`: Preparation
- `X.Y.Z-1`, `X.Y.Z-2`, ...: Work commits
- `X.Y.Z`: Close-out (bare version, no suffix)

**Preparation is optional.** A lightweight cycle — no ladder,
no setup commit — skips `-0` and starts at `-1` (its first
Work commit). The same holds at every level: a sub-cycle
needing no Preparation omits its `.0` (see Nesting). One that
grows a Preparation later adds the `0` step without
renumbering siblings.

Disambiguation:

- `-10` — Work commit #10 (final identifier `10`), not a
  Preparation.
- `-1.0` — Preparation of the `-1` sub-cycle (final
  identifier `0`).

**Nesting.** Sub-cycles append another level, recursively:

- `X.Y.Z-3.0` — Preparation of the `-3` sub-cycle
- `X.Y.Z-3.1`, `X.Y.Z-3.2` — its Work
- `X.Y.Z-3` — its Close-out
- `X.Y.Z-3.1.0` — Preparation of the `-3.1` sub-sub-cycle

Bump the version-of-record at the start of each phase, so the
active phase is recorded — and, per the preference above,
every commit carries a distinct version.

content.text:
Holding the edit, since you closed with thoughts-only and because question 4 below could rewrite some of the very lines I would be converting. Say go and versioning.md's 17 get swept in a minute.

**Why they survived, factually.** There was never a repo-wide conversion. Hard rule 8 plus prose.md's "applies going forward; existing text converts when touched" is the whole mechanism, and the one sweep we ran (`docs: typeable punctuation only`) was scoped to the parked branch's re-scoped set. Counting tracked markdown right now: 880 instances across 19 files. `notes/chores/chores-02.md` alone has 181, `notes/design.md` 85, `notes/done.md` 28, `notes/versioning.md` 17. Even nominally swept files are not clean: root `README.md` has 5, `TODO.md` has 1 (a stray `×`). `cycle-protocol.md` is the one at zero. So versioning.md was never in scope, and "we removed all of them" was true only of the going-forward rule.

**On a `[[N]]` in Done pointing at the commit: the path already exists, and it is two hops.** A Done entry's ref lands on the chores section header, and the as-built ladder is the first content under it, carrying the commit URL plus the 40-hex SHA. Making Done point at a commit directly would either replace that (losing the narrative and the rest of the cycle's commits) or add a second ref, which copies a SHA into a second file's References and doubles the backfill obligation, and then those refs migrate again when the entry retires to done.md. Same duplicate-fact-drifts argument that killed the chores edit list.

The better answer is that **the title is now the commit reference.** It is bold at the front of the entry, verbatim-identical to the commit title, and `git log --grep "<title>"` is zero hops, needs no backfill, cannot go stale, and works offline. notes.md already relies on exactly that for re-syncing a rewritten commit.

**You are right about the backfill debt, and the two cases differ.** `## feat: dynamic warmup`'s rungs are on `main`, so their SHAs are permanent and they are backfillable *now*; they should have been filled by the next push, which was this bookmark's first commit, and were not. `## docs: experiment in the local agent-files` is correctly waiting, since `agent-files-model` has not landed and notes.md forbids recording a SHA a rebase could invalidate. Worth noting how the miss happened: our `cycle.md` has backfill only as close-out step 6, and the 20260802 baseline added it as per-commit step 4 "Close the records" precisely because we reported this gap to the family on 2026-07-31. The gap we reported bit us in the next cycle because we have not synced the fix.

**"Should ladders have versions?" I think yes, for the as-built ladder only, and this reverses part of what I drafted.** The split is principled rather than convenient:

- **In-flight ladder: no.** Pre-landing the version is not final and the rung would be naming a step, which is the fragility we removed.
- **As-built ladder: yes.** There the version is not an identifier, it is a *recorded property of a landed commit*, sitting next to its SHA. We already record SHAs without objection, and the version has the same staleness profile and the same recovery path (`git log --grep`) that notes.md already specifies for a rewritten permanent commit.

What makes me fairly confident: it gives us the decoder table for free. The residue problem is someone holding a pasted report banner that says `iiac-perf 0.24.0` with no way to read it, and `custom.md` currently does that job by hand for two renumbered versions. An as-built ladder carrying title plus version plus SHA is that table, generated as a side effect of work we already do. And the timing is elegant: **the version enters the record at the same beat as the SHA, at backfill, when both are final.** No new discipline.

It also answers your `[[N]]` question, which is why the two converge: one hop from Done lands you on title plus version plus SHA in one place, with one backfill and no duplicated fact.

If we adopt it, the redraft is `notes.md`'s rung form and example, cycle-protocol's Chores sections rung form, the carve-out in prose.md's "no version in ... a chores header or as-built ladder", plus the specimen-vs-use sentence we already agreed was missing, and the chores narrative. All files this step already touches.

**The plain version:** the em dashes survived because there was never a repo-wide sweep, only a going-forward rule, and 880 remain across 19 files. Do not add a commit ref to Done entries; the bold title already gets you to the commit with `git log --grep`, for free and forever. Your ladder question is a good catch and I would change my own draft: keep versions out of the live ladder, put them into the as-built ladder at backfill time beside the SHA, where a version is a recorded fact rather than a name, and where it doubles as the decoder for old report banners. And yes, dynamic warmup's rungs are backfillable now and were missed.

Confirmed — and one correction: those rungs **are** on `main`. All eight are ancestors of `main` (the trapezoid rewrite landed them and the `dynamic-warmup` bookmark was deleted), so their versions and SHAs are final and backfillable right now. **Your Done-entry model is already what the rules say.** One `## Done` entry per cycle, its `[[N]]` landing on the chores `##` header, whose first content is by rule the as-built ladder. A markdown list has no anchor of its own, so the header is the only targetable spot, and "points to the ladder" is satisfied by the ladder being immediately under it. Multi-step or single-step makes no difference: a single-commit cycle is a one-rung ladder. Nothing to change.

**One revision to what I said last turn.** I proposed the version enters the rung at backfill, "same beat as the SHA". Your pasted ladders show the file already writes it at rung-open, and that is better: the version is known when the rung is written, the SHA is not, so each goes in when it is known. They share only the *correction* beat, since a rewritten commit invalidates both and re-syncs via `git log --grep`. Practical consequence: your two pasted ladders are already in the target form, and there is no rework.

## Recording the version-of-record

Where the version-of-record lives, how it's stored and
surfaced, and how often it changes — pick the case that fits
your medium:

- **Manifest** — where the version-of-record is stored:
  - if Rust, `Cargo.toml` `[package].version`
  - if Python, `pyproject.toml` `[project].version` (or the
    committed config it's sourced from)
  - otherwise wherever the medium records it (a generic
    `version.toml`, a book's frontmatter, …) — add the case as
    needed
- **Notation** — how the `-` form is stored:
  - if the format allows `-` (TOML `version.toml`, `Cargo.toml`),
    store it verbatim
  - if it bars `-` (PEP 440's local segment, e.g. a Python
    project), remap to `+` — `0.3.0-5.3.0` → `0.3.0+5.3.0`: same
    version, just the stored spelling
- **Reporter** — how a built artifact surfaces the
  version-of-record:
  - if a CLI app, `<cli-app> -V`
  - if a TUI/GUI, add to Help/About or display on the title
- **Cadence** — how often to bump: see
  [Unique per commit](#unique-per-commit-preference-not-requirement);
  this project follows the per-commit preference.

## Unique per commit (preference, not requirement)

Our general notion is that the version-of-record should change
on **every commit**, so a built or running artifact identifies
the exact commit it came from.

- This is a preference, **not** a hard requirement. A project
  following the cycle protocol may bump less often — once per
